How to Apply: Detailed Application Form

Candidates whose roll numbers are in the provisional list must complete the following steps to move forward in the selection process:

  1. Log in to the RPSC recruitment portal using your SSO ID.

  • After document verification by the department, the list of eligible candidates will be sent back to RPSC.
  • RPSC will then issue the final result and recommend the names of selected candidates to the concerned department for appointment.

CSBC Bihar Police Selection Process 2026

Selection for Prohibition Constable, Jail Warder, and Mobile Squad Constable follows three stages, governed by the respective Bihar cadre recruitment rules for each post:

  1. Written Examination - candidates scoring below 30% are not considered for the next stage.
  2. Physical Efficiency Test (PET) and Physical Standard Test (PST) - includes physical measurements and efficiency tests such as running, long jump, and high jump.
  3. Document Verification - for candidates who qualify PET/PST.

Candidates were shortlisted for PET/PST at up to five times the number of vacancies in each reservation category, reducible where enough eligible candidates were not available. A total of 19,681 candidates have been shortlisted for this stage, spread across three separate merit lists:

  • List 1 - Ex-Servicemen candidates qualified for PST.
  • List 2 - Home Guard candidates qualified for PET.
  • List 3 - General/direct-recruitment candidates (all categories, including women, transgender, and Freedom Fighter Ward candidates) qualified for PET.

Also Read: APPSC ATWO Syllabus 2026

How to Check and Download CSBC Bihar Police Result 2026

  1. Visit the official CSBC website: csbc.bihar.gov.in.
  2. Go to the "Results" or "Advertisement 03/2025" section on the homepage.
  3. Open the PDF titled for PET/PST result under Advt. No. 03/2025, dated 18 August 2026.
  4. Use Ctrl+F (or the search option on a mobile browser) to find your roll number.
  5. Check whether your roll number appears in List 1, List 2, or List 3, and confirm your category and post.
  6. Download and save the PDF for future reference.

What's Next After the CSBC Bihar Police Result 2026?

Shortlisted candidates must now prepare for the Physical Efficiency Test (PET) and Physical Standard Test (PST). A few points to keep in mind:

  • The PET/PST schedule, venue, and admit card release date have not yet been announced by CSBC. Candidates should keep checking the official website for updates.
  • Participation in PET/PST is mandatory for all shortlisted candidates; a missed attempt generally does not get a second chance in this type of recruitment.
  • Ex-Servicemen candidates in List 1 are required for PST (physical measurement), while other categories go through both PET and PST as applicable to their post and quota.

SBI CBO Final Result 2026: What the PDF Says

The official final result notice, signed by the General Manager, states that the listed roll numbers belong to candidates provisionally selected as Circle Based Officers. The selection is explicitly subject to two conditions mentioned in the PDF:

  • Qualifying the Proficiency Test in Local Language(s)
  • Fulfilment of eligibility criteria and conditions as prescribed in Advertisement No. CRPD/CBO/2025-26/18 dated 29.01.2026

This means candidates whose roll numbers appear in the list have not yet received a final, unconditional offer - the Local Language Proficiency Test and document/eligibility verification are still pending. KEA VAO Kannada Language Test Admit Card 2026: The Karnataka Examinations Authority (KEA) has notified the Compulsory Kannada Language Test 2026 for Village Administrative Officer (VAO) candidates from the outside-Karnataka and Kalyana Karnataka quota, along with candidates for several other Group-A and Group-B posts and the Police Constable post. This page explains the confirmed exam date, who must appear, the exam pattern, and the current status of the admit card, based on KEA's official notification.

Direct Link to Download KEA VAO Kannada Language Test Admit Card 2026

KEA VAO Kannada Language Test Admit Card 2026 - Quick Overview

Particulars Details
Conducting Body Karnataka Examinations Authority (KEA)
Notification Number ED/KEA/02/Recruitment/2026
Notification Date 11th August 2026
Test Name Compulsory Kannada Language Test
Applicable Post (among others) Village Administrative Officer (VAO) – Revenue Department
Test Date 22nd August 2026 (Saturday)
Test Timing 3:00 PM to 5:00 PM
Total Questions 100 (MCQ)
Maximum Marks 150
Qualifying Marks 50 out of 150
Official Website kea.kar.nic.in / cetonline.karnataka.gov.in

Important Dates

  • Notification issued: 11th August 2026
  • Kannada Language Test: 22nd August 2026 (Saturday), 3:00 PM – 5:00 PM
  • Main VAO written exam (General/RPC cadre): 4th October 2026
  • Main VAO written exam (Kalyana-Karnataka cadre): 25th October 2026

Also Read: RPSC 1st Grade Result 2026

Who Needs to Appear for the Kannada Language Test?

This test is not the main VAO recruitment exam. It is a qualifying-only requirement under Government Order No. Siasu 102 Sevana 2022 dated 18.03.2025, applicable to outside-Karnataka and Kalyana Karnataka quota candidates who have already qualified in the main written examination for their post, and who fall into any of the following categories:

  • Did not study Kannada as a subject up to SSLC or an equivalent/higher examination
  • Did not pass SSLC (or a higher exam) with Kannada as the medium of instruction
  • Have not previously cleared a Kannada Language Test conducted by a competent authority

Besides VAO and Village Accountant posts, the same 22nd August 2026 test date applies to candidates for the following posts:

  • Police Constable (CAR / DAR / KSRP / IRB / KSISF)
  • Land Surveyor
  • KREIS Teacher posts
  • Section Officer, Karnataka State Legal Services Authority

KEA VAO Kannada Language Test Admit Card 2026: Current Status

As of 19th August 2026, KEA's official notification confirms the exam date and reporting time for the Kannada Language Test. A separately branded admit card or hall ticket download link specific to this test has not been officially confirmed as active yet. This information is not available in the current notification. Candidates should keep checking the official KEA recruitment portal regularly, since KEA typically activates hall ticket downloads a few days before the exam date using the candidate's application/registration number.

How to Check for the Admit Card

  1. Visit the official KEA candidate portal: cetonline.karnataka.gov.in/KEA_EXAM_PORTAL.
  2. Look for the Kannada Language Test 2026 admit card or hall ticket link under the recruitment/admit card section, once activated.
  3. Log in using your Application Number and Date of Birth (or password, as specified by KEA).
  4. Verify your name, photograph, exam centre, and reporting time carefully.
  5. Download the admit card as a PDF and keep 2–3 printed copies.

Documents to Carry for the Kannada Language Test

  • Printed copy of the admit card (once released)
  • A valid original photo ID proof Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Voter ID, Passport, or Driving Licence

Important Instructions

  • Only candidates who have already qualified in the main written examination for their respective post are eligible to appear for this test.
  • Clearing the Kannada Language Test alone does not guarantee final selection it is a mandatory clearance step for the candidates it applies to.
  • Reach the exam centre well before the reporting time and carry only the items permitted under KEA's exam-day instructions.
  • Since this test covers multiple posts (VAO, Police Constable, Land Surveyor, KREIS Teacher, Section Officer), candidates should confirm their own exam centre and category-specific instructions on the admit card once it is issued.

IOB Apprentice Admit Card 2026: Important Instructions

  • Carry a clear printed copy of the IOB Apprentice Call Letter along with an original photo ID such as Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Voter ID, Passport, or Driving Licence.

  • Do not carry mobile phones, smartwatches, calculators, Bluetooth devices, or any study material into the examination hall, if attending at a physical centre.
  • Ensure your photograph, signature, and other personal details on the admit card are clearly visible before exam day.
  • If the exam is remote-proctored, ensure a working device with a front camera, microphone, and stable internet connection, as per the instructions on your specific call letter.

If any discrepancy is found on the admit card, candidates should act promptly:

The interview call letter is a mandatory document for the SBI CBO Recruitment 2026 drive, which is being conducted to fill 2,050 vacancies for the Circle Based Officer post across various states and language zones. Without this call letter, candidates will not be permitted entry into the interview venue, so downloading and verifying it well in advance is essential.

Carrying the correct set of documents is non-negotiable for interview-day entry. This section lists everything you must bring along.

  • A valid original photo ID proof (Aadhaar, PAN, Passport, Voter ID, etc.)
  • Original and photocopies of educational certificates and mark sheets
  • Recent passport-size photographs (the same one used during application, if specified)

Candidates should keep all documents organized in a single folder to avoid last-minute confusion at the venue.

SBI CBO 2026 Selection Process Explained

Understanding how your final selection is calculated helps you prepare strategically for the interview. This section explains the complete selection methodology for SBI CBO 2026.

The SBI Circle Based Officer recruitment follows a multi-stage selection process:

  1. Online Examination - The first screening stage testing candidates' aptitude and knowledge.
  2. Screening/Shortlisting - Candidates are shortlisted based on online exam performance for the interview stage.
  3. Interview - Worth 50 marks, assessing banking awareness, professional knowledge, and communication skills.
  4. Local Language Proficiency Test - Candidates must demonstrate proficiency in the regional/local language relevant to their applied state or circle.

How Is the Final Merit List Prepared?

The final selection isn't based on the interview alone it combines scores from multiple stages using a fixed weightage formula.

The final merit list for SBI CBO 2026 is prepared using combined weightage:

  • Online Examination: 75% weightage
  • Interview: 25% weightage

This means strong performance in the online exam significantly boosts your overall chances, but a good interview score remains essential for the final cutoff.

Eligibility Criteria

Candidates must meet the educational qualification, age limit, and nationality conditions set by the Central Bank of India to be eligible for the Apprentice post.

Educational Qualification

  • A graduation degree (bachelor's degree) in any discipline from a recognised university or institute.
  • Candidates should have completed graduation on or after 1 January 2022 (some sources indicate the cut-off as 1 January 2021; candidates should verify the exact date on the official notification).
  • Candidates with one year or more of work or training experience after graduation are not eligible, since this scheme is meant for fresh graduates.
  • Candidates who have already completed apprenticeship training, or are currently undergoing apprenticeship training elsewhere, are not eligible.
  • Basic computer knowledge is required.
  • Candidates must be proficient in the local language of the state they are applying for.

Age Limit

Candidates must be between 20 and 28 years of age as on 31 May 2026, meaning they should be born between 31 May 1998 and 31 May 2006 (both dates inclusive).

Candidates should check the official notification for the exact category-wise age relaxation applicable to them.

Salary / Stipend Details

Selected apprentices will receive a fixed monthly stipend of ₹15,000 during the 12-month training period. This is a training stipend rather than a regular salary, and no other allowances or benefits are provided. Completion of the apprenticeship does not guarantee permanent employment with the bank.

Application Fee

The exact application fee amount for the CBI Apprentice Recruitment 2026 was not confirmed in the sources reviewed for this article. Selection Process

The Central Bank of India Apprentice selection process involves two stages:

  1. Online Written Examination: An objective-type computer-based test with no negative marking for wrong answers.
  2. Local Language Proficiency Test: Candidates who qualify the online exam may need to appear for a test assessing reading, writing, and speaking skills in the local language of the applied state. Candidates who studied the local language at Class 10 or Class 12 level may be exempted from this test, subject to document verification.

Final selection also depends on document verification and meeting the required medical fitness standards set by the bank.

Documents Required at the Exam Centre

  • Printed copy of the CBI Apprentice Admit Card 2026
  • A valid original government-issued photo ID proof, such as Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Passport, Voter ID, or Driving Licence
  • A photocopy of the photo ID for verification
  • Recent passport-size photographs, as specified in the admit card instructions

Candidates should ensure the name on their ID proof matches the name printed on the admit card to avoid denial of entry.

How to Download the CBI Apprentice Admit Card 2026

Follow these steps to download your Central Bank of India Apprentice hall ticket:

  1. Visit the official website of the Central Bank of India at centralbankofindia.co.in or centralbank.bank.in.
  2. Go to the "Recruitment" or "Careers" section on the homepage.
  3. Click on the "CBI Apprentice Admit Card 2026" or "Download Call Letter" link.
  4. Enter your Registration Number/Roll Number and Password or Date of Birth.
  5. Fill in the captcha code, if required.
  6. Click the Login or Submit button.
  7. Your CBI Apprentice Hall Ticket 2026 will appear on the screen.
  8. Carefully verify all details, including your name, photograph, signature, exam date, and exam centre.
  9. Download the admit card and take a clear printout on an A4 sheet for the examination.

The online written examination consists of 100 objective-type questions worth 100 marks, to be completed in 60 minutes, with no negative marking.

The Bank of Baroda Apprentice Online Examination 2026 is scheduled for June 21, 2026 (Sunday). Candidates should plan their travel to the allotted exam centre in advance and check their reporting time as mentioned on the admit card to avoid last-minute stress.

Credentials Required to Download BOB Apprentice Admit Card

Before logging in to the admit card portal, keep the following details ready. This information is typically the same combination used during registration.

  • Registration Number / Roll Number
  • Password or Date of Birth (as set/used during application)
  • If you have forgotten your password, use the "Forgot Password" option on the login page to retrieve or reset your credentials.

How to Download Bank of Baroda Apprentice Admit Card 2026

This step-by-step guide explains the exact process to access and download your hall ticket from the official website, so you can complete it without confusion.

  1. Visit the official Bank of Baroda website: bankofbaroda.bank.in.
  2. Navigate to the "Careers" or "Current Opportunities" section on the homepage.
  3. Click on the link that reads "Bank of Baroda Apprentice Admit Card 2026."
  4. Enter your Registration Number/Roll Number and Password/Date of Birth in the login window.
  5. Click Submit to view your admit card on the screen.
  6. Check all the details carefully and download the admit card.
  7. Take a clear, color printout for use on exam day.

Details Mentioned on the Bank of Baroda Apprentice Admit Card

Once downloaded, candidates should cross-check every detail printed on the hall ticket immediately, since any discrepancy needs to be flagged to the bank well before the exam date.

The admit card typically includes:

  • Candidate's name, photograph, and signature
  • Registration number and roll number
  • Exam date, reporting time, and exam shift timing
  • Complete exam centre name and address
  • Important exam-day instructions and guidelines issued by the bank

Bank of Baroda Apprentice Exam Pattern 2026

This section explains how the BOB Apprentice online exam is structured, so candidates know exactly what to expect in terms of sections, marks, and timing.

The BOB Apprentice exam is an online objective-type test consisting of 100 questions for 100 marks, to be completed in 60 minutes. The paper is divided into four sections of equal weightage, with no sectional time limit unless specified otherwise in the official notification.

Section Number of Questions Marks
General / Financial Awareness 25 25
Quantitative & Reasoning Aptitude 25 25
Computer Knowledge 25 25
General English 25 25
Total 100 100

Key points about the exam pattern:

  • Each correct answer carries 1 mark.
  • There is no negative marking for wrong answers.
  • No marks are awarded for unattempted questions.
  • The question paper is available in English and Hindi, except for the General English section.

What to Carry on Exam Day

Carrying the right documents is essential, as candidates without a valid admit card or ID proof may be denied entry to the exam centre. This checklist covers what you must bring.

  • A clear, printed copy of the BOB Apprentice Admit Card 2026
  • A valid original photo ID proof (such as Aadhaar Card or PAN Card) the same ID used during the application process
  • A recent passport-size photograph
  • Arrive at the exam centre well before the reporting time mentioned on the admit card

What Happens After the Exam?

This section outlines the next stages of the selection process so candidates know what to expect once the online exam is over.

The Bank of Baroda Apprentice selection process does not end with the written exam. Candidates who qualify in the online test move to the following stages:

  1. Document Verification - Shortlisted candidates must produce original documents for eligibility verification.
  2. Language Proficiency Test - Candidates must demonstrate proficiency in the official local language of the state they applied for.
  3. Medical Examination - A final medical fitness check is conducted before confirmation of selection.

Selected apprentices will be engaged for a one-year apprenticeship period and will receive a stipend of ₹15,000 per month during this engagement.

RRB JE/DMS/CMA Selection Process 2026

Selection comprises four stages: 1st Stage CBT (CBT-I), 2nd Stage CBT (CBT-II), Document Verification (DV) and Medical Examination (ME).

CBT-I (Common for all posts) - 90 minutes, 100 Questions

Section Questions / Marks
Mathematics 30
General Intelligence & Reasoning 25
General Awareness 15
General Science 30
Total 100

CBT-II - 120 minutes, 150 Questions

Section Questions / Marks
General Awareness 15
Physics & Chemistry 15
Basics of Computers and Applications 10
Basics of Environment and Pollution Control 10
Technical Abilities (post/exam group specific) 100
Total 150
  • Negative marking: ⅓ mark deducted for each wrong answer in both CBTs.
  • Minimum qualifying marks: UR & EWS 40%, OBC-NCL 30%, SC 30%, ST 25% (relaxable by up to 2 marks for PwBD candidates where PwBD vacancies are short of eligible candidates).
  • CBT-II shortlisting: 15 times the community-wise vacancy per RRB, based on CBT-I merit.
  • DV shortlisting: equal to the number of vacancies, based on CBT-II merit using a normalized Merit Index across Exam Groups.
  • A virtual calculator is provided on-screen during CBT-II only.

How to Apply for RRB JE/DMS/CMA Recruitment 2026

  1. Visit the official RRB website or rrbapply.gov.in and Create an Account (mandatory personal mobile number and email ID; these cannot be changed later).
  2. Log in and select CEN No. 04/2026 (JE/DMS/CMA).
  3. Choose one RRB only and indicate zone/post preferences in order - this choice is final and cannot be changed.
  4. Fill in personal, educational and category details carefully.
  5. Complete live photo capture (webcam/front camera) as per the prescribed guidelines; upload signature (JPG/JPEG, 30–49 KB).
  6. Upload SC/ST certificate (PDF, under 400 KB) if opting for free train travel facility.
  7. Pay the applicable examination fee online (internet banking / debit-credit card / UPI).
  8. Submit the application; note down your Registration Number.
  9. Use the modification window (16.09.2026 to 25.09.2026) if corrections are needed, on payment of ₹250 per modification.
Important: Multiple applications to different RRBs, or multiple applications to the same RRB, will lead to rejection of all applications and debarment from future RRB/RRC exams.

Documents Required

  • Educational qualification certificates (diploma/degree, as applicable to the post) with date of issue
  • Matriculation/10th certificate (for name, DOB, father's/mother's name)
  • Category certificate (SC/ST/OBC-NCL/EWS/EBC), in prescribed Annexure format, from a competent authority
  • Ex-Servicemen declaration/employment certificate, where applicable
  • PwBD disability certificate and UDID, where applicable
  • Valid original photo ID (Aadhaar, Voter ID, PAN, passport, driving licence, etc.)
  • Recent colour passport-size photograph and running-handwriting signature
  • NOC from present employer (for those serving in Government/PSU), where applicable

Important Conditions

  • Only one application per candidate against this CEN is permitted; multiple applications lead to rejection and debarment.
  • Vacancies are provisional and may increase, decrease, or become nil, per Railway Administration requirements.
  • A candidate with more than one qualifying discipline may choose only one Exam Group, and is then eligible only for posts mapped to that group.
  • Medical fitness as per the prescribed Medical Standard (A-3/B-1/B-2/C-1, as applicable to the post) is mandatory; no alternative appointment is given if found unfit.
  • Once a category/post/RRB is allotted, candidates forfeit the right to be considered for any other post/category in the same pay level.
  • Use of unfair means, impersonation, or false information leads to lifetime debarment from RRB/RRC exams and possible legal action.

BOB Local Bank Officer Eligibility Criteria

Candidates must fulfil the following eligibility conditions, assessed as on the cut-off date of 01.08.2026, to apply for BOB Local Bank Officer Recruitment 2026.

Criteria Details
Nationality Citizen of India, or subject of Nepal/Bhutan, or a Tibetan refugee who came to India before 1 January 1962 with intent to permanently settle, or a person of Indian origin who migrated from specified countries (Pakistan, Burma, Sri Lanka, Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Zambia, Malawi, Zaire, Ethiopia, Vietnam) with intent to permanently settle in India
Educational Qualification Graduation in any discipline from a recognized University/Institution (mandatory)
Preferred Certifications IC 38 (Insurance Institute of India), NISM Series V-A (Mutual Fund Distributors), NISM Series XXI-A (PMS Distributors), NISM Series XIII (Common Derivatives)
Post-Qualification Experience Minimum 1 year as an Officer in any Scheduled Commercial Bank listed in the Second Schedule of the Reserve Bank of India
Language Proficiency Must be proficient (reading, writing, speaking, understanding) in the local language of the state applied for

Candidates who have resigned from an officer-grade position in Bank of Baroda, or exited the Bank while on contract within the last three years as on the cut-off date, are not eligible to apply. Employees currently working in Bank of Baroda in the officer cadre or on contract basis are also not eligible.

BOB Local Bank Officer Salary 2026

Selected candidates for the JMG/S-I grade will draw pay as per the following scale, along with allowances and benefits as per the Bank's policies.

Grade Pay Scale
JMG/S-I 48480-2000/7-62480-2340/2-67160-2680/7-85920

One advance increment will be granted to selected candidates who have one year or more of work experience as an Officer in a Scheduled Commercial Bank. Salary and other emoluments will be governed by the industry-level bipartite settlement and Joint Note applicable to bank officers, along with bank-specific allowances and perquisites as revised from time to time.

BOB Local Bank Officer Application Fee

The non-refundable application fee/intimation charges for BOB Local Bank Officer Recruitment 2026 are as follows. Fees must be paid irrespective of whether the candidate is shortlisted or the online test is conducted.

General, EWS & OBC Rs. 850/- (Inclusive of GST) + Payment Gateway Charges
SC, ST, PWBD, ESM/DESM & Women Rs. 175/- (Inclusive of GST) + Payment Gateway Charges

Payment can be made online through Debit Card, Credit Card, Internet Banking, or UPI.

BOB Local Bank Officer Age Limit

The age limit indicated below is for General category candidates as on the cut-off date of 01.08.2026.

  • Minimum Age: 21 years
  • Maximum Age: 30 years

Age Relaxation:

Category Age Relaxation
SC/ST 5 years
OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) 3 years
Persons with Benchmark Disabilities Gen/EWS - 10 years, OBC - 13 years, SC/ST - 15 years
Ex-Servicemen/Commissioned Officers (ECOs/SSCOs) with min. 5 years military service Gen/EWS - 5 years, OBC - 8 years, SC/ST - 10 years

There is no reservation for Ex-Servicemen in the Officers' Cadre; only age relaxation as above applies. OBC candidates in the "creamy layer" are not entitled to OBC reservation or age relaxation.

Candidates should ensure that they meet the prescribed age limit as on the specified cut-off date. You can use our Age Calculator to check your exact age and confirm your eligibility before applying.

BOB Local Bank Officer Selection Process

Selection for BOB Local Bank Officer Recruitment 2026 will be based on the following stages:

  • Online Test (multiple sections, described below)
  • Group Discussion (GD) and/or Personal Interview (PI)
  • Psychometric Test and/or any other assessment as deemed suitable by the Bank
  • Local Language Proficiency Test (LPT), where applicable

The tentative structure of the online examination is as follows:

Section Name of Test No. of Questions Maximum Marks Duration
1 English Language 30 30 30 Minutes
2 Banking Knowledge 30 30 30 Minutes
3 General/Economic Awareness 30 30 30 Minutes
4 Reasoning Ability & Quantitative Aptitude 30 30 30 Minutes
- Total 120 120 120 Minutes

The English Language section is qualifying in nature only, and marks scored in it will not count towards the final merit list. There is a penalty of 0.25 marks for each wrong answer. The minimum qualifying marks for GD/PI are 60% for General category and 55% for Reserved category candidates. Candidates must qualify in the Local Language Proficiency Test unless they have studied the local language at the 10th or 12th standard level.

  • Bank of Baroda LBO Syllabus 2026

How to Apply for BOB Local Bank Officer Recruitment 2026

Eligible candidates can apply online for BOB Local Bank Officer Recruitment 2026 by following the steps below.

  1. Visit the official Bank of Baroda website: www.bankofbaroda.bank.in
  2. Go to the Career section/webpage and click on "Current Opportunities".
  3. Register online and fill in the application form for Local Bank Officer.
  4. Upload the required documents, including scanned photograph, signature, resume, DOB proof, educational certificates, work experience certificates, and caste/PWBD certificate (if applicable).
  5. Verify all details carefully before submission, as no changes are allowed after clicking Submit.
  6. Pay the application fee online using Debit Card, Credit Card, Internet Banking, or UPI.
  7. Take a printout of the completed application form and fee receipt for future reference.

BOB Local Bank Officer Important Instructions

  • Candidates can apply for only one state; multiple applications will result in forfeiture of fees for extra registrations.
  • No change of category is permitted at any stage after registration of the online application.
  • Candidates must possess a valid personal email ID and mobile number, kept active till completion of the recruitment process.
  • Candidates are advised to possess or acquire a valid Aadhaar card, as Online Aadhaar verification will be conducted at various stages.
  • Biometric data/IRIS scan and photograph will be captured and verified before the online examination, at GD/interview, and at the time of joining.
  • Mobile phones, pagers, calculators, or similar devices are not allowed inside the examination premises.
  • Selected candidates will be posted within the state applied for the first 12 years of service or until promotion to SMGS-IV grade, whichever is earlier.
  • Selected candidates will be on probation for 12 months from the date of joining.
  • Selected candidates must execute a Service Bond to serve a minimum of 3 years, or pay an amount equivalent to three months' gross salary (not exceeding Rs. 2 Lakhs) if they leave before completing three years of service.
  • Any legal disputes arising from this recruitment fall under the exclusive jurisdiction of courts/tribunals in Mumbai.

IOCL Executive Recruitment 2026 Eligibility (Post-wise)

1. Graduate Engineer (Grade A)

Full-time regular B.Tech/BE/equivalent degree from an AICTE/UGC-recognized institution in one of the following domains: Chemical, Civil, Computer Science & IT, Electrical, Electronics & Communication, Instrumentation, or Mechanical Engineering.

2. Officer (Marketing) – Grade A

Full-time 2-year MBA / PGDBA (equivalent to MBA as per AIU) with specialization in Marketing Management. General/EWS/OBC(NCL): 60% marks minimum; SC/ST/PwBD: 55% marks minimum. The specialization must be reflected on the final degree certificate.

3. Law Officer (Grade A)

Graduate degree in any discipline plus LLB, OR a 5-year Integrated LLB, recognized by the Bar Council of India. General/EWS/OBC(NCL): 60% marks in each qualifying degree; SC/ST/PwBD: 55% marks. Minimum 2 years of post-qualification work experience (as on 30.06.2026) is required in litigation, law firms, or legal functions with private/public organizations or government, in areas such as litigation, arbitration/ADR, or drafting and vetting of legal/contractual documents.

4. Assistant Quality Control Officer (Grade A0)

Master’s degree in Chemistry (Inorganic/Organic/Analytical/Physical/Applied/Industrial Chemistry). General/EWS/OBC(NCL): 60% marks minimum; SC/ST/PwBD: 55% marks minimum. Minimum 2 years of post-qualification experience in Testing/R&D/Quality Control in a petroleum, petrochemical, polymer, or fertilizer laboratory, and/or in an NABL-accredited lab (Chemical discipline, Lubricants/Petroleum group).

5. Diploma Engineer (Grade E0)

3-year full-time Diploma in Engineering (Electrical, Mechanical, or Safety-related disciplines as listed in the official notification). General/EWS/OBC(NCL): 65% marks minimum; SC/ST: 55% marks minimum. Candidates possessing higher professional qualifications such as BE/B.Tech, MBA, CA, CS, CMA, MCA, or Ph.D. are not eligible for this post. For the Safety discipline, an additional Diploma in Industrial Safety (minimum 1 year) is required.

Important: For the Diploma Engineer (Safety) post, PwBD candidates are not eligible, as the notification states this is a hazardous-industry role involving critical safety operations.

  • Qualifications acquired through Part-time/Correspondence/Distance/Online learning modes are not eligible.

Selection comprises three stages: Computer Based Test (CBT), Group Discussion (GD) & Group Task (GT), and Personal Interview (PI).

  • Each question carries 1 mark; 0.25 marks deducted for every incorrect answer.
  • Section order is fixed - Section A first, then Section B.
  • CBT will be held at 83 test centers across India (city list available in the official notification and syllabus link below).

How to Apply for IOCL Executive Recruitment 2026

  1. Visit the official website www.iocl.com and click "Apply Online."
  2. Choose "Click here for New Registration" and enter Name, contact details, and email ID to generate a Provisional Registration Number and Password.
  3. Log in and fill the application form; use "Save and Next" to save progress at each stage.
  4. Upload scanned photograph (4.5cm x 3.5cm, 20–50 KB), signature (10–20 KB), and left thumb impression (20–50 KB) as per specifications.
  5. Capture a live photograph via webcam or mobile phone as prompted by the portal.
  6. Fill in educational, category, and other required details.
  7. Preview the form carefully, then click "Complete Registration" - no changes are allowed after this step.
  8. Proceed to the Payment tab and pay the application fee online.
  9. Click "Submit" and download/print the completed application form and e-receipt for your records.
Important: Only one application per post is allowed; in case of multiple applications, the latest one is treated as final. SC/ST/PwBD candidates are exempt from the application fee; all other candidates must pay ₹1,000 + GST.

Documents Required

  • Qualifying degree/diploma certificate and mark sheets (as applicable to the post)
  • CGPA-to-percentage conversion certificate, if applicable
  • Work experience proof (for Law Officer and Assistant Quality Control Officer posts) on organizational letterhead

  • PwBD certificate and UDID card, where applicable
  • Valid photo identity proof (PAN/Passport/Driving License/Voter ID/Aadhaar, etc.)
  • No Objection Certificate (NOC) from current employer, if presently employed in Government/PSU/Autonomous Body

Important Conditions

  • Candidates having their graduation/diploma in combined, integrated, or interdisciplinary subjects (e.g., Mechatronics, Robotics) are not eligible for the Graduate Engineer or Diploma Engineer posts.
  • No change of category (Gen/EWS/SC/ST/OBC(NCL)/PwBD) is permitted once submitted in the online application.
  • Selected candidates will be placed anywhere in India, including overseas offices, at Corporation discretion.
  • Final selection is provisional and subject to subsequent verification of certificates, testimonials, and medical fitness.
  • Candidates must clear Pre-Employment Medical Examination (PEME) guidelines before joining.
  • Any use of unfair means, impersonation, or misconduct during the process will lead to disqualification and may result in debarment from future IOCL examinations.
  • IOCL reserves the right to cancel, restrict, enlarge, modify, or alter the recruitment/selection process without prior notice.

BPSC TRE-4.0 Eligibility 2026

Basic Eligibility

  • Candidate must be a citizen of India.
  • Candidate must hold the educational and training qualification prescribed by the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE) for the relevant school level, as detailed in the official notification. For special school teacher posts, qualification recognised by the Rehabilitation Council of India (RCI) is required.

Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) Requirement

School Level Required Qualifying Test
Primary (Class 1–5) CTET Paper-I or BTET Paper-I
Middle (Class 6–8) CTET Paper-II or BTET Paper-II
Secondary (9–10) & Special School Teacher STET Paper-I
Higher Secondary (11–12) STET Paper-II
Teachers appointed and working before 2012 who have passed the Dakshata Pariksha (competency exam) are exempted from the TET requirement. Candidates who hold the required educational qualification and are appearing in the Secondary Teacher Eligibility Test (STET, 2026) may also apply, but must pass STET 2026 before the Preliminary Examination; the admit card for the Preliminary Examination will not be issued if STET 2026 is not cleared.

Qualification Snapshot by School Level

  • Primary (1–5): Senior Secondary (or equivalent) with a two-year Diploma in Elementary Education, OR Senior Secondary with 4-year B.El.Ed., OR Graduation with a two-year Diploma in Elementary Education, OR Graduation/Senior Secondary with two-year D.Ed. (Special Education), as per NCTE norms.
  • Middle (6–8): Graduation with a two-year Diploma in Elementary Education, OR Graduation/Post-Graduation with B.Ed., OR 4-year B.A./B.Sc.Ed. or B.A.Ed./B.Sc.Ed., with the requisite subject combination for Language, Math & Science, or Social Science teachers as specified in the notification.
  • Secondary (9–10): Graduation/Post-Graduation in the relevant subject group with minimum 50% marks and B.Ed. from an NCTE-recognised institution.
  • Higher Secondary (11–12): Post-Graduation in the relevant subject (as per the subject-combination table in the notification) with minimum 50% marks and B.Ed., or equivalent qualification recognised by NCTE.
Important: The exact subject-wise postgraduate/graduate combinations, computer science qualification pathways, physical education pathways, and language-subject provisions for Urdu/Bangla/Sanskrit/Madrasa Board qualifications are extensive and vary by post - candidates must verify their specific eligibility against Sections 2(A) to 2(R) of the official notification before applying.

Category Maximum Age

Note: Divyang (PwD) candidates get 10 years' age relaxation; ex-servicemen get 3 years plus actual service period, provided actual age does not exceed 57 years on the date of application. Serving Bihar government employees get 5 years' relaxation, capped at a maximum of 5 competitive-exam attempts under this relaxation. Panchayati Raj/Nagar Nikay institution teachers have relaxed age limits. Superannuation age is 60 years.

BPSC TRE-4.0 Pay Scale 2026

School Level Pay
Primary (Class 1–5) Starting pay level ₹25,000 per month plus other admissible allowances
Middle (Class 6–8) Starting pay level ₹28,000 per month plus other admissible allowances
Secondary (Class 9–10) Basic pay ₹31,000 per month plus other admissible allowances
Higher Secondary (Class 11–12) Basic pay ₹32,000 per month plus other admissible allowances
Service and cadre category: School Teacher, non-gazetted (अराजपत्रित) in all four levels.

BPSC TRE-4.0 Selection Process

Selection is made in two stages - a Preliminary Examination and a Main Examination. There is no interview.

Stage 1: Preliminary Examination

  • Objective-type General Studies paper; all questions carry equal (1) marks.
  • Duration: 2 hours; Total marks: 150.
  • Each question offers 5 options (A, B, C, D, E); candidates must mark one option. Option (E) must be chosen if the candidate does not wish to attempt the question.
  • Negative marking: 1/3 mark deducted for each wrong answer, and 1/3 mark deducted for any question left unanswered without selecting option (E).
  • Covers general science, current national and international events, Indian history and Bihar's history, general geography, Bihar's geographical features, India's polity and economy, the freedom movement and Bihar's contribution, and general mental ability.
  • Minimum qualifying marks: General category 40%, BC 36.5%, EBC 34%, SC/ST/women/Divyang candidates 32% (with an additional 4% horizontal relaxation for women, subject to a minimum of 32%, applicable only to Bihar domicile candidates).
  • Number of candidates shortlisted for the Main Examination will be 2.5 to 10 times the total advertised vacancies, category-wise, based on merit.

Stage 2: Main Examination

Paper School Level Structure Marks
Paper 1 Primary (1–5) Part I – Language (qualifying, min 30%); Part II – General Studies 150
Paper 2 Middle (6–8) Part I – Language (qualifying); Part II – General Studies; Part III – Subject Paper 150
Paper 3 Secondary (9–10) & Special School Teacher Part I – Language (qualifying); Part II – General Studies; Part III – Subject Paper 150
Paper 4 Higher Secondary (11–12) Part I – Language (qualifying); Part II – General Studies; Part III – Subject Paper 150
  • Objective (MCQ) type, duration 2 hours for each paper; each question carries 1 mark.
  • Negative marking: 1/3 mark deducted for each wrong or unanswered question (same 5-option format as the Preliminary Exam).
  • Language paper (Part I) is qualifying only, with a minimum of 30% required; it does not count towards merit.
  • Same category-wise minimum qualifying marks apply as in the Preliminary Examination (General 40%, BC 36.5%, EBC 34%, SC/ST/women/Divyang 32%).
  • Merit is prepared from Main Exam marks - Part II only for Primary (1–5); Part II + Part III combined for all other levels. There is no re-evaluation.
Note: Guest teachers (Atithi Shikshak) meeting prescribed eligibility get service-based weightage marks of 5 marks per year of service, up to a maximum of 25 marks, added to their qualifying score in both the Preliminary and Main Examinations, per the applicable court orders and Education Department resolutions.

How to Apply for BPSC TRE-4.0 Recruitment 2026

  1. Visit the official BPSC OTR portal bpsconline.bihar.gov.in.
  2. Complete One Time Registration (OTR) via the "New User Registration" button using a valid, active email ID and mobile number (mandatory for all BPSC exams).
  3. After OTR, sign in to DigiLocker's Meri Pehchan portal (create a new account if you don't have one) and give consent to link your documents with the application, or proceed directly to the online application via the browser back option.
  4. Log in at bpsconline.bihar.gov.in/candidate/login and complete your profile in six steps: Personal Information, Address Information, Other Information, Qualification Information, Experience Information, and Photo/Signature Upload.
  5. Upload a live webcam photograph and scanned signatures in both Hindi and English.
  6. Review all entries, tick the declaration checkbox, and click "Submit and Lock Profile" (profile details cannot be edited after locking, except by unlocking before final submission).
  7. Go to the "New Application" tab, select this advertisement (No. 14/2026), choose your post/subject and up to 38 preferred districts in order of priority.
  8. Pay the applicable fee online (SBI Payment Gateway) and confirm payment.
  9. Click "Proceed to Application" and then "Submit Application" to finalise your form.
  10. Download and print the confirmed Application Form from the "My Account" tab for future reference.
Important: Once fee payment is completed, the selected post/subject cannot be changed unless the payment is cancelled and the entire process is repeated. Cancelled payments and cancelled applications are not eligible for any refund or chargeback claim.

Documents Required

  • Matriculation certificate (proof of date of birth)
  • Educational and professional/training qualification certificates and mark sheets as per the applied post
  • CTET/BTET/STET (Paper-I or Paper-II, as applicable) qualifying certificate and mark sheet
  • RCI-issued valid CRR number and certificate (for special school teacher posts)
  • 6-month special/inclusive education training certificate (where applicable)
  • Category certificate (SC/ST/EBC/BC), with caste and domicile certificate
  • EWS certificate in the prescribed format, where applicable
  • Disability (Divyang) certificate issued/countersigned by a government medical college or civil surgeon, where applicable
  • Ex-servicemen certificate, where applicable
  • Freedom fighter grandchild/great-grandchild relationship certificate, where applicable
  • Transgender identity proof certificate issued by the competent authority, where applicable
  • Guest teacher experience and appointment certificates issued by the District Education Officer, where weightage is claimed
  • Valid photo identity card, as declared in the application
  • 4 recent passport-size photographs
  • Printed copy of the submitted Preliminary/Main exam application and e-Admit Card

Important Conditions

  • Candidates can apply for a maximum of 38 districts, listed in order of preference; the merit list and posting will follow district priority against category-wise availability.
  • A candidate may take part in this recruitment examination a maximum of 5 times, as per the Bihar Vidyalaya Adhyapak (Appointment, Transfer, Disciplinary Action & Service Conditions) Amendment Rules, 2024.
  • Reservation benefits are applicable only to candidates who are original/domiciled residents of Bihar.
  • Candidates must select only one subject - the one in which they have qualified the relevant Teacher Eligibility Test (CTET/BTET/STET).
  • Reserved-category candidates applying against unreserved posts will not receive reserved-category age or qualifying-mark relaxations.
  • There is no provision for re-evaluation of the objective-type Main Examination.
  • Merely submitting the online application does not guarantee candidature; final eligibility will be decided based on documents furnished by the candidate.
  • Provisional merit lists will be verified by the Education Department against submitted documents; the merit list may be revised based on this verification.
  • No supplementary result will be published after the provisional result is declared.
  • The Commission reserves the right to modify, postpone or cancel the recruitment process.

BEML Apprentice Eligibility Criteria

Candidates who possess the required educational qualification and have passed their final examination within three years from the closing date of application are eligible to apply.

Qualification Category Applicable Trades/Disciplines
Graduate (Technical) – 4-yr Full Time Engineering Mechanical, Electrical Electronics, Civil, Computer Science, Electronics & Communication, Automobile, Information Science, E&T, AI & ML, Aeronautical
Graduates (General) – 3-yr Full Time Graduation B.Sc, B.Com, BCA, BBA, BBA(HR)
Diploma – 3-yr Full Time Electrical Electronics, Civil, Computer Science, Electronics, Communication, Automobile, Instrumentation, Mechanical Engineering
ITI – Full Time (2 Year/1 Year based on trade) Fitter, Welder, Turner, Machinist, Electrician, COPA, Mechanic Diesel, Carpenter, Tool & Die Making, Sheet Metal, Plumber, Mechanic Auto Electrical & Electronics, MMV, Electronic Mechanic

Candidates are NOT eligible to apply in the following cases:

  • Awaiting the results of their final examination.
  • Not completed 17 years of age.
  • Have undergone or are undergoing apprenticeship training in any organization for any duration.

Please note:

  • Candidates must possess a full-time regular degree/diploma qualification from a recognized institute/university. Qualifications acquired through part-time/correspondence/distance education/online mode are not eligible.
  • Candidates should have passed out not before three years from the closing date of application; the date of result declaration should be clearly mentioned in the mark sheet, or supported by a certificate from the college/university.
  • The percentage of marks in the final examination of the qualifying degree (not semester-wise) should be mentioned in the final/consolidated mark sheet. If CGPA is mentioned, candidates must upload the Percentage Conversion Letter issued by their institute/university.
  • The required area of specialization (major/dual, if applicable) should be mentioned in the degree/diploma certificate; if not, a supporting certificate/letter from the college/institute/university is required.

Also Read: IOCL Executive Recruitment 2026 Notification Out - Apply Online for 470 Engineers, Officers and More Posts

BEML Apprentice Stipend 2026

Selected apprentices will receive a monthly stipend based on their qualification category, subject to satisfactory performance and attendance.

Sl. No. Apprenticeship Trade Category Monthly Stipend
1 Graduate (Technical) – 4-yr Full Time Engineering Rs. 12,300/-
2 Graduates (General) – 3-yr Full Time Graduation Rs. 12,300/-
3 Diploma – 3-yr Full Time Rs. 10,900/-
4 ITI – Full Time (2 Year/1 Year based on trade) Rs. 9,600/- or Rs. 10,560/- (based on trade)

Poor performance or unauthorised absence may result in termination from the apprenticeship program. The total tenure of apprenticeship training is one year from the date of joining, co-terminated with completion of the one-year duration; no further extension is permitted.

BEML Apprentice Application Fee

There is no application fee for BEML Apprentice Recruitment 2026. There is also no written examination or interview process for applicants.

BEML Apprentice Age Limit

  • Applicants must be Indian citizens and 17 years old or above at the time of application.
  • Candidates who have not completed 17 years of age are not eligible to apply.

No upper age limit is specified in the notification.

Before submitting the application, candidates are advised to verify that they meet the required age criteria. Use our Age Calculator to calculate your exact age as per the official cut-off date.

BEML Apprentice Selection Process

  • Applications will be screened as per eligibility criteria and prescribed qualification.
  • A category-wise merit list will be prepared for each trade at each location, in the ratio of 1:5 times the number of training slots notified.
  • Incomplete or ineligible applications will be summarily rejected without any intimation.
  • Reservation is applicable for SC/ST/OBC(NCL) as per the Apprentices Act 1961 and Apprenticeship Rule 1992, as amended from time to time.
  • Shortlisted candidates will be called for document/certificate verification in order of merit, in a ratio of 1:5 with respect to the training slots notified/available. Communication will be through the candidate's registered email. No TA/DA will be paid for the document verification process.
  • A merit list will be prepared based on candidates found suitable at document verification, in order of the percentage of marks obtained in the final qualifying examination.
  • Offer of Engagement will be issued immediately to eligible candidates, subject to availability of training slots; remaining eligible candidates will be placed on a Reserved Waiting Panel, maintained at five times the training slot strength.
  • The Reserved Waiting Panel will be replenished periodically in merit order as vacancies arise.
  • Candidates will be engaged in merit order upon accepting the tri-partite apprenticeship contract on the NATS/NAPS website, and submission of a medical certificate (prescribed format) and police verification certificate.

BEML Apprentice Documents Required

  • Apprenticeship Registration/Enrolment Number under NATS/NAPS with a 100% completed/updated profile on the portal.
  • Scanned copies of educational certificates and mark sheets (clearly visible/readable).
  • Proof of age (Matriculation Certificate).
  • SC/ST/latest OBC(NCL) caste certificate as per Government of India formats (if applicable).
  • Bank cancelled cheque/first page of passbook (DBT-enabled account details).
  • Recent colour passport-size photograph and signature.
  • Identity card issued by the Government of India (e.g., Aadhaar, Passport, Driving License, PAN Card, etc.).

Candidates must have an active Aadhaar-seeded bank account that is DBT-enabled for Direct Benefit Transfer, as per Government of India norms. The Name and Date of Birth of the applicant must match across the Matriculation (10th Class) Certificate, Aadhaar Card, and bank account.

How to Apply for BEML Apprentice Recruitment 2026

Step 1: Candidates must first register themselves (as a candidate/student) on:

  • NAPS for ITI trades at https://apprenticeshipindia.gov.in, or
  • NATS for Degree/Diploma in Engineering at https://nats.education.gov.in/

and complete/update their profile by uploading all required documents.

Step 2: After obtaining the NAPS/NATS registration/enrolment number, candidates should apply on the BEML website as follows:

  1. Visit https://recruitment.bemlindia.in
  2. Go to Apprentices → Login/Registration
  3. Fill in the application form with the required details, including NAPS/NATS enrolment number and DBT-enabled bank account details.
  4. Upload all required documents as specified.
  5. Submit the application online before the last date.

Applications must be submitted online through the official BEML website only; no other mode of application will be accepted. There is no application fee, written examination, or interview process for applicants.

Also Read: RRB JE 04/2026 Recruitment 2026 Notification Out - Apply Online for 4029 Junior Engineer Posts

BEML Apprentice Important Instructions

  • Candidates are permitted to submit only one application in a particular trade at a particular location.
  • Candidates submitting multiple applications, or applying for more than one location/trade, will not be considered and their applications will be summarily rejected.
  • Incomplete applications or those submitted without proper documents will be summarily rejected without any intimation.
  • Candidates found ineligible, or providing false information/documents that are not in order, will be disqualified at any stage during the engagement process or during the period of engagement.
  • Completion or undergoing of the apprenticeship program does not entitle the apprentice to any claim for employment with BEML.
  • Apprentices are not allowed to enrol in or undergo any regular course/job during their apprenticeship tenure.
  • Apprentices must maintain a weekly work-diary and submit it to the assigned reporting officer; they must also maintain confidentiality of BEML's proprietary information and adhere to the company's code of conduct.
  • Any Intellectual Property (inventions, discoveries, or works) created by apprentices during the apprenticeship will be the property of BEML.
  • BEML reserves the right to terminate the apprenticeship at any time for reasons including absenteeism, indiscipline, misconduct, poor performance, or violation of company policies.
  • BEML will not entertain any claims of injury/accident, theft, or other loss during the course of apprenticeship training.
  • Management reserves the right to amend the terms and conditions at any time; apprentices will be notified via email or official communication channels. BEML's decision will be final and binding.

Railway Recruitment Cell, North Central Railway (RRC NCR) has extended the last date to apply online for RRC NCR Act Apprentice Recruitment 2026. As per the official notice dated 15.08.2026, the online application window for engagement of Act Apprentices (2026-27) has now been extended to 31.08.2026 (23:59 hrs), following the addition of new trades to the originally notified slots.

RRC NCR had originally invited online applications from 08.07.2026 for a total of 1853 slots under the Apprentices Act, 1961, for training at various Divisions and Workshop units under North Central Railway. The original closing date of 07.08.2026 has now been extended to accommodate the newly added trades notified on 14.08.2026.

Quick facts: RRC NCR is conducting engagement of Act Apprentices for training year 2026-27 across 1853 originally notified slots (now revised with additional new trades) at Prayagraj, Agra, Jhansi Divisions/TMC-Line and Jhansi Workshop under North Central Railway. Applicants aged 15 to below 24 years (as on 07.07.2026) can apply online through www.rrcpryj.org. The extended last date to apply online is 31.08.2026 (23:59 hrs).

RRC NCR Act Apprentice Eligibility Criteria

Candidates meeting the age and educational eligibility for the designated trades can apply. The eligibility details are as follows:

Educational Qualification:

  • Candidates must have passed SSC/Matriculation/ 10th Class or its equivalent (under the 10+2 system) with a minimum of 50% aggregate marks from a recognized Board.
    Candidates must possess an ITI Certificate/National Trade Certificate (NTC) in the relevant trade issued by NCVT/SCVT recognized by the Government of India.
    Possession of a valid NCVT/SCVT-affiliated ITI Certificate in the relevant trade is mandatory.

Domicile: As per RRC/NCR notified criteria

RRC NCR Act Apprentice Age Limit

  • Minimum Age: 15 years
  • Maximum Age: Should not have completed 24 years (as on 07.07.2026)

Age Relaxation:

Category Age Relaxation
SC/ST 5 years
OBC 3 years
Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD) 10 years
Ex-servicemen Up to additional 10 years, to the extent of service rendered in Defence Forces, plus 3 years, provided a minimum of 6 months' service at a stretch has been completed (further conditions not fully available in the source document)

Candidates should ensure that they fulfill the prescribed age criteria. Calculate your exact age using our Age Calculator before submitting your application to confirm your eligibility.

How to Apply for RRC NCR Act Apprentice Recruitment 2026

  1. Visit the official RRC NCR website: https://www.rrcpryj.org
  2. Read all instructions in the notification carefully and confirm eligibility before applying.
  3. Create a valid personal email ID, if not already available, and maintain it until the end of the entire engagement process.
  4. Register and fill in the online application form for Act Apprentice engagement against the revised slots/new trades.
  5. Submit the application online well before the extended closing date of 31.08.2026 (23:59 hrs) to avoid last-minute website load issues.

Note: Detailed step-by-step application instructions, application fee, required documents, and the selection process are available on the official RRC NCR website but are not specified in the documents provided for this article.

RRC NCR Act Apprentice Important Instructions

  • This is a centralized notification for engagement of Act Apprentices under the Apprentices Act, 1961, for North Central Railway; RRC/NCR has been nominated as the nodal agency for obtaining online applications.
  • Applications can be submitted only online on RRC's official website, https://www.rrcpryj.org; candidature will be considered only on the basis of information filled in the online application.
  • New trades have been added to the originally published slots; the revision was notified on the official website on 14.08.2026.
  • Interested and eligible candidates can apply online against the revised slots/new trades up to the extended last date of 31.08.2026 (23:59 hrs).
  • Applicants are advised to submit their online application well before the closing date to avoid failure due to heavy load or website jam.

What Is a Bharat Sarkari Job?

A Bharat Sarkari Job is any government job opportunity offered across India's central and state government departments - spanning all 28 states and 8 union territories. The term "Bharat" simply emphasises pan-India coverage: a Bharat Sarkari Job notification could originate from a central body like the SSC, UPSC, or Indian Railways, or from a state public service commission recruiting for state-level posts. Regardless of origin, these roles share the defining traits Indian aspirants seek - long-term job security, government pay scales, and statutory retirement benefits.

Sarkari Job vs Private Job

A sarkari job differs from private-sector employment in a few important ways: government positions are governed by service rules that protect against arbitrary termination, salaries follow Pay Commission recommendations rather than market negotiation, and employees are entitled to pension schemes (NPS or OPS depending on recruitment year), medical coverage under CGHS, and fixed working hours. Private jobs, by contrast, often offer higher starting pay in competitive fields but carry less structural job security.

Sarkari Bharat Vacancies by Sector

Sarkari bharat vacancies span several major recruiting sectors. Each sector below links to a dedicated hub page with sector-specific notifications, eligibility criteria, and exam patterns.

Banking Jobs (IBPS, SBI, RBI)

Banking recruitment includes IBPS PO, IBPS Clerk, SBI PO, SBI Clerk, RBI Assistant, and NABARD postings. These roles are among the most competitive sarkari bharat jobs, offering strong starting pay and clear promotion tracks. Browse current openings on our Banking Jobs hub.

Railway Jobs (RRB NTPC, ALP, Group D)

Indian Railways is the country's largest single recruiter, with RRB NTPC, Group D, ALP, JE, and Technician posts opening in large batches. Check live Railway vacancies on our Railway Jobs hub.

Defence Jobs (Army, Navy, Air Force)

Defence recruitment covers Indian Army (including Agniveer), Navy, Air Force, BSF, CRPF, CISF, and ITBP postings. See ongoing openings on our Defence Jobs hub.

Teaching Jobs (KVS, NVS, State Boards)

Teaching sarkari jobs include KVS, NVS, DSSSB, and state education board recruitment for TGT, PGT, and PRT posts. Explore current teaching vacancies on our Teaching Jobs hub.

SSC & UPSC Notifications

SSC (CGL, CHSL, MTS, GD) and UPSC (Civil Services, CDS, NDA) notifications remain the most closely tracked central-government exams. Full notification archives are available on our SSC Jobs and UPSC Jobs hubs.

Sarkari Job Find - Filter by Qualification & State

Not every sarkari job requires a degree. Use the qualification and state filters below to sarkari job find openings that actually match your eligibility, instead of scrolling through listings you don't qualify for.

Several high-volume recruiters - including Railways (Group D), SSC (MTS, GD), and state police departments - recruit primarily at the 10th pass and 12th pass level. Browse these openings on our 10th & 12th Pass Jobs page.

Sarkari Job for Graduates & Postgraduates

Graduate and postgraduate-level sarkari jobs include SSC CGL, Bank PO, UPSC Civil Services, and various state PCS exams. See qualification-matched listings on our Graduate Jobs page.

State-Wise Sarkari Bharat Job (Bihar, UP, Tamil Nadu, and more)

State government recruitment is listed separately by state, since eligibility and domicile rules vary. Find your state's current openings via our State Government Jobs directory.

सरकारी फॉर्म ऑनलाइन 2026 कैसे भरें? (How to Apply Online)

हर साल लाखों उम्मीदवार सरकारी फॉर्म ऑनलाइन 2026 भरने की प्रक्रिया में गलतियाँ कर बैठते हैं, जिससे उनका आवेदन रद्द हो सकता है। नीचे दी गई सरल प्रक्रिया से आप अपना फॉर्म सही तरीके से भर सकते हैं।

आवेदन की चरणबद्ध प्रक्रिया

  1. संबंधित विभाग की आधिकारिक अधिसूचना (Notification PDF) ध्यान से पढ़ें और अपनी पात्रता जांचें।
  2. वैध ईमेल आईडी और मोबाइल नंबर से पोर्टल पर पंजीकरण (Registration) करें।
  3. व्यक्तिगत विवरण, शैक्षणिक योग्यता, और आवश्यक दस्तावेज़ अपलोड करें (फोटो, हस्ताक्षर, प्रमाणपत्र)।
  4. निर्धारित आवेदन शुल्क का ऑनलाइन भुगतान करें और भुगतान की रसीद सुरक्षित रखें।
  5. फॉर्म सबमिट करने से पहले सभी जानकारी की दोबारा जांच करें और फॉर्म का प्रिंटआउट अवश्य लें।

Documents Required for Sarkari Form

Typical documents needed: recent passport-size photograph (as per specified size/format), scanned signature, educational certificates and mark sheets, category certificate (if applicable), and a valid ID proof (Aadhaar/PAN).

Common Mistakes to Avoid While Applying

  • Submitting a photo or signature that doesn't match the specified pixel/size requirements.
  • Missing the last date due to server load - apply at least 2–3 days before deadline.
  • Entering a name or date of birth that doesn't match your certificates exactly.
  • Forgetting to download and save the final submitted form and payment receipt.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is a Bharat Sarkari Job?

A Bharat Sarkari Job refers to any government job opportunity across India's central and state departments - including Railways, Banking, SSC, UPSC, Defence, Police, and PSUs - offering job security, fixed pay scales, and pension benefits under government service rules.

How can I get instant Sarkari Job Alert notifications?

You can bookmark this page for daily updates, or subscribe to OnlyJobs's notification service to receive a Sarkari Job Alert as soon as a new central or state vacancy is announced.

Where can I check the latest Bharat Job Result 2026?

All declared results - including written exam results, merit lists, and interview outcomes - are listed in the Results section of this page, updated as soon as departments release official Bharat Job Result notices.

How do I find a Sarkari Job that matches my qualification?

Use the qualification filters on this page to sarkari job find openings suited to 10th pass, 12th pass, diploma, graduate, or postgraduate candidates, sorted by sector and state.

सरकारी फॉर्म ऑनलाइन 2026 में आवेदन कैसे करें?

सबसे पहले संबंधित विभाग की आधिकारिक अधिसूचना पढ़ें, पात्रता जांचें, फिर वैध ईमेल और मोबाइल नंबर से रजिस्ट्रेशन करके फॉर्म भरें, दस्तावेज़ अपलोड करें और आवेदन शुल्क जमा करें।

Is OnlyJobs reliable for sarkarijob updates?

Yes - OnlyJobs has tracked sarkarijob notifications since 2011, cross-verifying every listing against official department websites before publishing.

What is the difference between a Sarkari Job and a private-sector job?

Sarkari jobs offer government-backed job security, pension (NPS/OPS), fixed working hours, and statutory benefits, while private jobs typically offer market-driven pay with fewer long-term security guarantees.

Anganwadi Recruitment 2026 – FAQ's

How to apply for Anganwadi Recruitment 2026 online?

Visit your state's official WCD / ICDS portal (link provided in table above). Register with mobile & Aadhaar, fill the application form, upload documents (photo, 10th certificate, Aadhaar, domicile), and submit before the last date. Print the application acknowledgement slip after submission.

What is the eligibility for Anganwadi Worker 2026?

Candidates must have passed 10th or 12th standard from a recognized board. Age limit is 18–35 years (varies by state). Must be a permanent resident of the ward/village for which vacancy exists. Only female candidates are eligible for Worker and Helper posts.

What is the salary of Anganwadi Worker in 2026?

Anganwadi Worker receives a monthly honorarium of ₹10,000–₹20,000 depending on the state (Karnataka and TN are highest at ~₹14,000). Anganwadi Helper gets ₹5,000–₹7,000/month. The Central Government pays ₹4,500/month as base honorarium, and states add their own component on top.

Is there a written exam for Anganwadi jobs?

No, there is no written examination for Anganwadi Worker and Anganwadi Helper posts. Selection is purely merit-based on academic qualification marks (10th / 12th percentage). For Supervisor / CDPO posts, a written exam or interview may be conducted depending on the state.

What is the age limit for Anganwadi Helper?

Age limit is 18 to 35 years as of 1st January 2026 in most states. SC/ST candidates get 5 years relaxation (maximum age 40). OBC candidates get 3 years relaxation (maximum age 38). PwD candidates get additional relaxation as per state rules.

What documents are required for Anganwadi job application?

Required documents: Aadhaar card, 10th/12th marksheet and certificate, domicile/residence certificate, caste certificate (SC/ST/OBC), passport-size photograph, scanned signature, and EWS/PwD certificate if applicable. Graduation certificate is needed for Supervisor post applications.

What is ICDS recruitment 2026?

ICDS stands for Integrated Child Development Services - the government programme under which Anganwadi centres operate nationwide. ICDS recruitment 2026 refers to hiring of Anganwadi Workers, Helpers, Supervisors, and CDPOs by state WCD departments under the Ministry of Women & Child Development (wcd.nic.in).

Is Anganwadi Worker a permanent government job?

Anganwadi Workers and Helpers are honorary workers, not regular government employees. They receive a fixed monthly honorarium (not salary) and are entitled to benefits like ESI, health insurance, and maternity benefits. Supervisors and CDPOs are regular government employees in most states and receive full pay & grade pay.

Can I apply for Anganwadi job from a different district?

No. Anganwadi Workers and Helpers must be permanent residents of the same ward/village/district where the vacancy exists. A domicile or residence certificate is mandatory. Applications from outside the specified locality are rejected. For Supervisor/CDPO posts, the same district residency rule generally applies.

Forest Department Posts List

The forest department offers a range of posts across different levels, from ground-level field roles to gazetted officer positions. Most current openings on this page are for Group C posts - Forest Guard, Forester, Beat Guard, and Field Guard - making this a common landing point for anyone searching forest department group c recruitment 2026.

  • Forest Guard - entry-level field post responsible for forest protection and anti-poaching patrols
  • Forester - supervises Forest Guards and manages a forest beat or range sub-unit
  • Forest Beat Officer - field-level post combining patrol, record-keeping, and community liaison duties; commonly searched as forest beat officer notification 2026
  • Range Forest Officer (RFO) - manages an entire forest range, includes administrative and enforcement responsibilities
  • Assistant Conservator of Forests (ACF) - gazetted officer post, typically recruited through state forest service exams
  • Indian Forest Service (IFS) Officer - recruited through UPSC, the highest field-level forestry cadre in India

Eligibility for Forest Department Jobs 2026

Educational Qualification

  • Forest Guard / Forest Watcher / Field Guard: 10th or 12th pass from a recognized board
  • Forester: 12th pass, often with Science subjects; some states require a diploma in Forestry
  • Range Forest Officer: Graduate degree, frequently in Science, Agriculture, or Forestry
  • ACF / IFS: Graduate degree in a relevant discipline (Botany, Zoology, Forestry, Agriculture, Veterinary Science, Engineering, or Environmental Science), followed by the respective state or UPSC exam

Age Limit & Relaxation

The general age limit for Forest Guard and Forester posts is usually 18–27 years, though this varies by state. Age relaxation is generally available for SC/ST (5 years), OBC (3 years), PwBD candidates, and other reserved categories as per government norms.

Reservation & Age Relaxation for Ex-Servicemen

Most state forest departments reserve a fixed percentage of Forest Guard, Forester, and Beat Guard posts for ex-servicemen, in addition to SC, ST, OBC, and EWS reservations. Candidates applying for jobs for ex servicemen in forest department typically receive:

  • Additional age relaxation, usually 3–5 years beyond the general age cap (or as per length of military service)
  • Relaxed physical standards in several states
  • A reserved vacancy quota, separate from the general merit list

Exact quota percentages and relaxation norms differ by state, so always cross-check the specific notification before applying.

Physical Standards

Most Forest Guard and Forester posts require candidates to clear height, chest measurement (for male candidates), and a Physical Efficiency Test involving running, walking, or trekking - since the job involves regular field patrol duty in forest terrain.

Selection Process & Exam Pattern for Forest Officer & Forest Guard Posts

The selection process for forest department recruitment generally involves multiple stages, designed to test both academic knowledge and physical fitness given the field nature of the job.

Written Exam, PET/PST & Document Verification

  1. Written Examination - objective-type questions on General Knowledge, General Science, Reasoning, Mathematics, and sometimes Forestry/Environment-related topics
  2. Physical Efficiency Test (PET) / Physical Standard Test (PST) - running, walking/trekking distance, height and chest measurement
  3. Document Verification - verification of educational certificates, age proof, category certificates, and (where applicable) ex-servicemen discharge documents
  4. Medical Examination - fitness check before final appointment
  5. Final Merit List - based on combined written exam and PET/PST scores, as per each state's weightage formula

Syllabus Highlights for Forest Guard & Ranger

  • General Knowledge & Current Affairs
  • General Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology basics)
  • Basic Mathematics / Numerical Ability
  • Reasoning & Mental Ability
  • State-specific General Knowledge (local geography, forests, wildlife sanctuaries)
  • For Ranger/RFO level: Forestry science, environmental laws, and wildlife protection acts

How to Apply for Forest Department Recruitment 2026 (Apply Online)

Follow these steps to complete your forest department recruitment 2026 apply online process:

  1. Visit the official website of the respective state Forest Department or recruitment board (link provided in the notification table above)
  2. Register using your mobile number and email ID to generate login credentials
  3. Fill in the online application form with personal, educational, and category details
  4. Upload scanned copies of your photograph, signature, and required certificates
  5. Pay the application fee online via net banking, debit card, or UPI (fee varies by category and state)
  6. Review all entered details carefully before final submission
  7. Submit the form and download/print the confirmation page for future reference

Documents Required & Application Fee

Documents required:

  • Passport-size photograph and signature (scanned, as per specified format)
  • Educational certificates and mark sheets
  • Date of birth proof (10th certificate or birth certificate)
  • Category certificate (SC/ST/OBC/EWS), if applicable
  • Ex-servicemen discharge certificate, if applying under that quota
  • Domicile/residence certificate, where required by the state

Application fee: Typically ranges from ₹200–₹1,000 depending on the state and category, with fee concessions or exemptions commonly available for SC/ST, PwBD, and ex-servicemen candidates.

FAQs - Forest Department Recruitment 2026

Q1: What is the latest forest department recruitment 2026?

The latest notifications include Forest Guard, Forester, Range Forest Officer, and Group C forest posts released by state forest departments, PSCs, and staff selection boards. Check the table above for live vacancies and last dates, updated daily.

Q2: What is the last date to apply for forest department recruitment 2026?

The application last date varies by state and recruiting body - it is listed against each notification in the table above under "Last Date to Apply." Always confirm the exact date on the official notification before applying.

Q3: What is the qualification for forest guard recruitment 2026?

Most Forest Guard and Field Guard posts require a 10th or 12th pass from a recognized board. Higher posts like Forester or Range Forest Officer typically need 12th pass, a graduate degree, or a degree in a science/forestry-related field.

Q4: Is there any age relaxation for ex-servicemen in forest department recruitment?

Yes. Jobs for ex-servicemen in the forest department usually come with reserved vacancies and additional age relaxation - typically 3 to 5 years beyond the standard age limit - along with relaxed physical standards in many states.

Q5: How can I apply online for forest department vacancy 2026?

Visit the official website of the respective state forest department or recruitment board, register with your basic details, fill in the application form, upload the required documents, pay the fee, and submit. Full step-by-step details are in the "How to Apply" section above.

Q6: Which states have active forest guard recruitment 2026 notifications?

States including West Bengal, Punjab, Tamil Nadu, Himachal Pradesh, and Tripura currently have or regularly release forest guard and forest officer vacancies. See the state-wise section above for details on each.

Q7: What is the salary for forest guard and forest officer posts in 2026?

Forest Guard salary typically ranges from ₹28,000 to ₹35,000 gross per month under Pay Level 3, while Range Forest Officer and ACF posts range from ₹50,000 to ₹95,000 depending on pay level. Full breakdown is in the salary table above.

Q8: Is there a written exam for forest guard recruitment 2026?

Yes, most states conduct a written exam covering General Knowledge, General Science, Reasoning, and Mathematics, followed by a Physical Efficiency Test (PET) and document verification before the final merit list is prepared.
