Two Types of No Exam Govt Jobs

No-exam recruitment in India falls into two patterns, and knowing which one a notification belongs to tells you exactly what to prepare for:

Type Typical Posts Who it's for How Selection Works
Fresher - no exam, usually no interview Apprentice, GDS, trainee 10th/12th/ITI/Diploma/Graduate pass Merit list prepared from academic marks
Experienced - no exam, interview-based Officer, manager, specialist, medical Professionals with relevant work experience Shortlisting based on qualification/experience, followed by a personal interview

How Recruitment Without Exam Works in Government Jobs

This section explains the different routes through which government departments fill vacancies without conducting a written competitive exam.

1. Direct Recruitment

Certain senior and specialised posts - such as Chairman, Member, and Secretary in Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) and State Public Service Commissions (PSCs) - are filled through direct recruitment based on eligibility criteria like qualifications, experience, and domain expertise, rather than a written exam. Similarly, some administrative posts in the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) may be filled through direct recruitment.

2. Sports Quota Recruitment

Government organisations such as Indian Railways, the Indian Army, and Public Sector Banks reserve a quota of posts for candidates with outstanding achievements in sports at the state, national, or international level. Eligible candidates can be appointed to posts like Assistant Station Master, Ticket Collector, and Clerk without going through the regular written exam.

3. Cultural Quota Recruitment

Indian Railways also recruits individuals with exceptional talent in arts, fine arts, music, or literature under the cultural quota for posts such as Junior Clerk, Ticket Collector, and Assistant Loco Pilot.

4. Internal Promotions and Deputation

Government departments, including the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) and Indian Police Service (IPS), promote existing employees to higher posts based on performance, seniority, and experience - without requiring them to clear a fresh competitive exam. Ex-servicemen and defence personnel are also often considered for civilian government posts through deputation or reservation quotas, without a written exam.

5. Apprenticeships and Trainee Programmes

Railways, PSUs, and central organisations like DRDO and BEL regularly hire Act Apprentices, Trade Apprentices, and Project Trainees through merit lists based on academic marks - with no written entrance test.

6. Walk-in Interviews

Some government and PSU organisations directly call candidates for walk-in interviews based on their qualifications and experience, especially for technical, medical, and contractual roles.

Government Jobs Without Exam by Sector

This section breaks down no-exam opportunities by sector - banking and railways - which are among the most common areas where such recruitment occurs.

Bank Jobs Without Exam

While most public sector bank recruitment (PO, Clerk, SO) happens through IBPS or bank-specific written exams, some banks fill specific posts - such as Local Bank Officer and certain Specialist Officer roles - through direct recruitment, where the bank shortlists applications based on eligibility criteria and conducts an interview instead of a written test.

Railway Jobs Without Exam

Indian Railways and the various Railway Recruitment Boards/Cells (RRBs/RRCs) offer no-exam entry through:

  • Act Apprentices (selection via academic merit list)
  • Sports Quota posts (Assistant Station Master, Ticket Collector, Clerk)
  • Cultural Quota posts (Junior Clerk, Ticket Collector, Assistant Loco Pilot)
  • Scouts and Guides Quota

Before You Apply: How to Spot Fake "No Exam" Job Offers

No-exam recruitment is the single biggest magnet for job fraud in India, because "direct joining, no exam" is exactly what scammers promise. Four rules protect you:

  1. No genuine government post is ever sold. Nobody - agent, "officer", consultancy - can arrange selection for money. The only payment in real recruitment is the application fee, paid on the official portal, typically a few hundred rupees.
  2. Verify the notification on the official domain. Every real notice lives on a .gov.in, .nic.in or official PSU domain. Every row in our list links to the post page where the official notification PDF and apply link are attached - if an offer you received isn't traceable to an official notice, treat it as fraud.
  3. No recruitment happens over WhatsApp or Telegram DMs. Forwarded "joining letters" and interview calls demanding a deposit are scams, full stop.
  4. Cross-check suspicious notices against PIB Fact Check before sharing or paying anything.

How to Apply for Government Jobs Without Exam

  1. Open the post from the live list and read the official notification PDF - eligibility, age limits and fee are final there, not in any summary.
  2. Confirm you match the qualification and category requirements before paying any fee.
  3. Apply on the official portal linked in the notification; keep the registration number and fee receipt.
  4. For merit-list posts (GDS, apprentice), enter marks exactly as on your certificates - mismatches reject applications at verification.
  5. Track the post page for merit list / shortlist updates, or subscribe to WhatsApp/Telegram alerts so deadlines and results reach you automatically.

Government Jobs Without Exam - FAQs

1. Are there really government jobs without an exam?

Yes. Apprenticeship intakes, India Post GDS, sports and cultural quota posts, walk-in interviews and direct recruitment for experienced candidates are all filled without a written competitive exam. The live list at the top of this page shows every such notification currently open.

2. Which government jobs have no exam and no interview at all?

India Post GDS and Railway/PSU Act Apprentice selections use only a merit list of academic marks - there is no written test and no interview. Everything depends on your Class 10 (and ITI/diploma, where applicable) percentage.

3. What no-exam options exist for freshers after 10th, 12th or ITI?

Apprenticeships, GDS and trainee posts are the main fresher routes. Selection is a merit list prepared from academic marks, which is why these notifications attract very high application volumes despite no exam.

4. Can experienced professionals get a government job without an exam?

Yes. PSUs and autonomous bodies fill officer, manager and specialist posts by shortlisting candidates on qualification and experience, followed by a personal interview - no written test.

5. Are government jobs without exam permanent?

Often not. Apprenticeships are roughly one-year training engagements with a stipend, and many walk-in posts are contractual with fixed tenure. Direct-recruitment posts can be regular - the notification states the nature of each post, so check before applying.

6. Are there bank jobs without an exam?

A few. Some banks fill specialist and local officer posts through shortlisting plus interview. Bank apprenticeship drives vary - some are merit-based while others include an online test - so read each notification's selection clause.

7. Are there railway jobs without an exam?

Yes: Act Apprentice intakes (merit list), sports quota, cultural quota and Scouts & Guides quota. Apprentice intakes are large; the quota routes are small zonal recruitments with their own assessment process.

8. Is India Post GDS really without an exam?

Yes - selection is an online merit list generated from Class 10 marks, with no exam and no interview. Because of that, GDS is heavily targeted by paid-selection scams; apply only through the official GDS portal.

9. How do I identify fake "no exam" job offers?

No genuine government post is sold, fees are paid only on official portals, and no recruitment happens over WhatsApp or Telegram messages. Verify every offer against the official notification on a government or PSU domain - if it isn't there, it's fraud.

10. How often is this list updated?

Daily. New notifications are added as they release, and every listing is removed automatically after its last date, so the list only ever shows posts you can still apply for.

Govt Jobs for Law Graduates - Eligibility (LLB, LLM, BL)

Eligibility varies by post, but the core requirement for almost every government law job is a recognised law degree. Senior and specialised roles add experience, an LLM, or Bar enrolment on top.

Educational Qualification

  • Bachelor of Law (BL) / LLB (Legum Baccalaureus): the baseline qualification for most legal and law officer posts.
  • LLM (Master of Laws): required for senior legal officer, faculty, and some advisory positions.
  • Integrated 5-year degrees - BA LLB, BBA LLB, BCom LLB - are accepted wherever an LLB is required.

The degree must be from a university recognised by the Bar Council of India.

Bar Council Enrolment & AIBE

For litigation, prosecutor, and standing-counsel roles you generally need to be enrolled as an advocate with a State Bar Council, and many positions ask for the All India Bar Examination (AIBE) Certificate of Practice issued by the Bar Council of India. Purely advisory or research posts (Law Clerk, Research Fellow, Legal Consultant) often do not require enrolment.

Age Limit & Relaxations

The upper age limit is typically 30 to 40 years for the general category, depending on the post and recruiter. Statutory relaxations apply: usually 3 years for OBC, 5 years for SC/ST, and additional relaxation for PwD and ex-servicemen candidates. Always confirm the exact limit and cut-off date in the official notification, as judicial-service and PSU limits differ.

Salary & Pay Scale for Government Law Jobs

Pay depends on the organisation and grade. Officer-level legal posts under the 7th Pay Commission generally fall in Pay Levels 10 to 12, with a monthly salary roughly between ₹56,100 and ₹1,77,500, plus Dearness Allowance, House Rent Allowance, and other benefits. PSU legal officers are paid on IDA scales, which can be higher at entry grade.

Types of Law Officer / Legal Posts in Government Sector

  • Judicial Services - Civil Judge (Junior Division), Additional District Judge, High Court Judge, recruited via State Judicial Service Exams (PCS-J)
  • Law Officer / Legal Officer - Roles in public sector banks (IBPS SO Law), insurance companies (LIC AAO Legal), regulatory bodies (SEBI Grade A Legal), and PSUs (Coal India, NTPC, GAIL Legal)
  • Legal Assistant & Legal Advisor - Administrative legal support roles in ministries, universities, and district courts
  • Assistant Public Prosecutor (APO) - Prosecution roles recruited through State PSCs, requiring LLB and often a minimum years of practice

Judicial Services (Civil Judge, ADJ, High Court Judge)

Judicial Services is the most prestigious and highest-paying career path for LLB graduates. Recruitment happens through State Public Service Commissions (e.g., RPSC, UPPSC, MPPSC) via a three-stage exam: Preliminary, Mains, and Interview. Civil Judge posts typically require 0-3 years of practice depending on the state, while some states allow fresh LLB graduates to apply directly.

Law Officer / Legal Officer (Banks, PSU, Insurance)

Public sector banks and insurance companies recruit Law Officers through specialist officer (SO) exams. These posts require only an LLB degree (AIBE not mandatory) and offer competitive pay scales under the 7th Pay Commission equivalent structure, along with allowances.

Legal Assistant & Legal Advisor Posts

These are typically Group B/C administrative-legal posts in ministries, universities, and PSU legal departments, requiring an LLB degree and sometimes relevant drafting/litigation experience.

Assistant Public Prosecutor (APO)

APO recruitment is conducted by State PSCs (e.g., RPSC Assistant Prosecution Officer) and requires an LLB degree, enrollment as an advocate, and in most states, a minimum period of practice (often 3 years).

Selection Process for Law Govt Jobs

The selection process differs by post but commonly includes:

  1. Written examination - testing legal knowledge, aptitude, and general awareness (for judicial services and most exam-based posts).
  2. Interview / viva-voce - assessing legal reasoning and suitability.
  3. Document verification - degree, Bar enrolment, AIBE, age, and category certificates.

Advisory and consultant posts are often filled by shortlisting and interview alone, without a written exam.

Law Govt Jobs FAQ's

What are the latest law govt jobs in 2026?

Current law government jobs in 2026 include Law Officer, Legal Officer, Assistant Prosecution Officer, Judicial Service, and Legal Adviser posts across High Courts, PSUs, public sector banks, and central/state departments. The table above is updated daily with vacancy count, last date, and the official notification link.

Which departments hire LLB and law graduates?

High Courts and District Courts, the Ministry of Law and Justice, UPSC, State Public Service Commissions, public sector banks, PSUs, insurance companies, and regulatory bodies regularly recruit law graduates for legal and judicial roles.

What is the eligibility for government law jobs?

Most posts require a Bachelor of Law (LLB/BL) from a recognised university; senior roles may require LLM and experience. Litigation and prosecutor posts usually require enrolment with a State Bar Council and, often, the AIBE certificate.

What is the salary of a Law Officer in the government sector?

A government Law Officer or Legal Officer typically earns between ₹56,100 and ₹1,77,500 per month under the 7th Pay Commission, depending on the organisation, plus DA, HRA, and allowances. PSU legal officers draw IDA-scale pay.

Can a fresher LLB graduate get a government job?

Yes. Freshers can apply for Civil Judge (Junior Division) judicial-service exams, Law Clerk and Research Fellow posts in High Courts, and trainee legal roles. Some PSU and bank Law Officer posts require a few years of post-enrolment experience.

How can I apply for law officer vacancies in central government?

Open the post in the table above, read the official notification, register on the recruiter's portal, fill in the application with your LLB and enrolment details, pay the fee, and submit before the last date.

What is the difference between Judicial Services and Law Officer posts

Judicial Services (Civil Judge, via state judiciary exams) places you on the bench as a judge. Law Officer/Legal Officer posts are departmental legal-counsel roles in PSUs, banks, and ministries - advisory and litigation support, recruited by interview or written test.

Is there an age limit for govt law jobs?

Most posts set the upper age at 30 to 40 years for the general category, with statutory relaxations for OBC, SC/ST, and PwD candidates. Check each notification, as judicial-service and PSU limits differ.

The Nainital Bank Limited (Nainital Bank), a private sector bank headquartered in Nainital, Uttarakhand, with a network of 178 branches across 5 states, has released a notification for the recruitment of Specialist Officers in Grade/Scale-I, II & III. This recruitment drive will fill 41 Specialist Officer posts across 14 specialized profiles including Risk Officer, HR Officer, IT Officer, Data Scientist/Analyst, Civil Engineer/Architect, Manager-Credit, Manager-Law, Manager-Risk, Manager-Company Secretary, Manager-Security Officer, and Senior Manager posts in Credit, Forex, Treasury, and Law. Interested and eligible candidates can apply online through the Bank's official career portal.

Nainital Bank Specialist Officer Vacancy 2026 (41 Posts)

A total of 41 Specialist Officer vacancies have been notified across Grade/Scale-I, II, and III. The post-wise vacancy and age criteria (as on 01.08.2026) are given below. Note: the number of vacancies is provisional and the Bank may fill vacancies as per its actual requirement.

Risk Officer Scale-I 02
HR Officer Scale-I 03
IT Officer – Software Developer / API Developer / RPA Developer / ETL Developer / System Administrator / Database Administrator / Network Administrator Scale-I 10
Data Scientist / Analyst Scale-I 02
Civil Engineer / Architect Scale-I 02

A candidate can apply for only one post. In case of multiple applications by the same candidate, only the latest valid (completed) application will be retained, and the fee paid for the other registrations will be forfeited.

Nainital Bank Specialist Officer Eligibility Criteria & Qualification

The educational qualification for every post must be full-time and regular, from a University accredited by UGC, or an AICTE-approved institute, or a Board recognized by the Government of India/approved regulatory bodies. Candidates who completed their education through Distance Mode, Open Schooling, Part-Time mode, Correspondence Courses, or Executive MBA mode are not eligible to apply.

Post Essential Qualification Post-Qualification Experience
Risk Officer (Scale-I) Full-time Postgraduate degree in MBA (Finance) / Master's in Mathematics/Statistics/Econometrics with min. 60% marks. Preference to candidates with certification in Risk in Financial Services (IIBF)/Integrated Risk Management (NIBM)/GARP-FRM-I or II/CFA 1 year as Risk Officer in Bank/NBFC/FI/Fintech (desirable)
HR Officer (Scale-I) Full-time Postgraduate degree in MBA with specialization in Personnel Management/Industrial Relations/HR/HRD/Social Work/Labour Law, min. 60% marks 1 year as HR Officer in Bank/NBFC/FI/Fintech (desirable)
IT Officer (various streams) Graduate in BE/B.Tech or Postgraduate in M.Tech/M.E./MCA in Computer Science/IT/Electronics & Communication/Data Science, min. 60% marks. Preference for proficiency in Python, JAVA, .NET, SQL 1 year in relevant field at Bank/NBFC/FI/Fintech (desirable)
Data Scientist / Analyst (Scale-I) Bachelor's or Master's degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Statistics, or related field, min. 60% aggregate 1 year working on large databases as Data Scientist/Analyst in Bank/NBFC/FI/Fintech (desirable)
Civil Engineer / Architect (Scale-I) Graduate in B.E./B.Tech in Civil Engineering, or Bachelor's Degree in Architecture, min. 60% marks 1 year in construction, maintenance, or project management in Bank/NBFC/FI/Fintech (desirable)
Manager-Credit (Scale-II) Full-time Graduate/Postgraduate degree in MBA (Finance). CA/CMA/CFA an added advantage Min. 3 years in Credit Department/handling credit portfolio in Bank/NBFC/FI/Fintech (mandatory)
Manager-Law (Scale-II) Full-time Bachelor's Degree in Law (LLB), enrolled as advocate with Bar Council. PG Law degree preferred Min. 3 years as Law Officer in Bank/NBFC/FI/Fintech (mandatory)
Manager-Risk (Scale-II) Full-time Graduate/Postgraduate in MBA (Finance)/Master's in Mathematics/Statistics/Econometrics. Preference for risk-related certifications Min. 3 years as Risk Officer in Bank/NBFC/FI, working in Bank/FI/NBFC/Fintech units (mandatory)
Manager-Company Secretary (Scale-II) Associate Member of the Institute of Company Secretaries of India (ICSI). LLB/CA/ICWA/CMA/FRM desirable Min. 3 years working as CS in Bank/NBFC/FI/Fintech (mandatory)
Manager-Security Officer (Scale-II) Bachelor's degree in any discipline Min. 5 years as Officer in Indian Army/Navy/Air Force not below rank of Captain, OR min. 5 years as Officer in Paramilitary not below rank of Deputy Commandant
Senior Manager-Treasury (Scale-III) Full-time Graduate in any discipline + PG in MBA/PGDBA/PGDBM/PGPM/PGDM with Finance specialization (min. 2 years duration), OR Master's in Statistics/Economics Min. 5 years in executing trades, managing asset-liability, interest rate risk, funding & liquidity in Bank/NBFC/FI/Fintech (mandatory)
Senior Manager-Forex (Scale-III) Full-time Graduate + MBA/PGDBA/PGDBM/PGPM/PGDM with specialization in Finance/International Business/Trade Finance (min. 2 years duration) Min. 5 years knowledge of currency markets, cross-currency swaps, forwards, trade finance, FEMA/FEDAI guidelines in Bank/NBFC/FI/Fintech (mandatory)
Senior Manager-Credit (Scale-III) Full-time Graduate + PG Degree in Finance. CA/CMA/CS/ICWA/CFA desirable Min. 5 years in credit-related operations/handling credit portfolio in Bank/NBFC/FI/Fintech (mandatory)
Senior Manager-Law (Scale-III) Full-time Bachelor's degree in Law, enrolled as Advocate with Bar Council. Master's degree preferred Min. 5 years working as Law Officer in Bank/NBFC/FI/Fintech (mandatory)

Where a university has awarded a CGPA/GPA and no percentage conversion criterion is specified, the percentage shall be calculated by dividing the total marks obtained by the candidate in all subjects across all semesters by the aggregate maximum marks in all subjects, irrespective of honours/optional/additional subjects. In case of experience, the relevant experience certificate must specifically mention experience in Banks/NBFCs/FIs/Fintech.

Ration Card and Learner's Driving License are NOT valid ID proof.

Graduation in any discipline from a recognized University, or any equivalent qualification recognized as such by the Central Government. Candidates in their final year/semester of graduation may also apply provisionally, subject to producing proof of having passed the graduation examination on or before 31.12.2026.

Matriculate Ex-servicemen who have obtained the Indian Army Special Certificate of Education, or the corresponding certificate in the Navy or Air Force, after completing not less than 15 years of service in the Armed Forces of the Union, are also eligible. Such certificates should be dated on or before 31.12.2026.

SBI Junior Associate Recruitment 2026 Reservation

  • 4% horizontal reservation is provided to Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD), as per Section 34 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, for categories including Blind/Low Vision, Deaf/Hard of Hearing, locomotor disabilities (one/both arms, one/both legs, cerebral palsy, leprosy cured, dwarfism, acid attack victims, muscular dystrophy, spinal deformity/injury), Autism Spectrum Disorder (mild), intellectual disability, specific learning disability, mental illness, and multiple disabilities.
  • 4.5% of total vacancies are reserved for Disabled Ex-Servicemen and dependents of servicemen killed in action, in addition to the 10% earmarked for Ex-Servicemen (a total of 14.50%). First priority in appointment goes to Disabled Ex-Servicemen, and second priority to dependents of defence personnel killed in action or severely disabled (over 50% disability attributable to defence services).
  • Reservation for PwBD/XS/DXS candidates is horizontal and is included within the vacancies of the various parent categories (SC/ST/OBC/EWS/GEN) to which the candidate belongs.
  • OBC vacancies are available only to candidates in the "Non-Creamy Layer"; OBC candidates in the "Creamy Layer" are not entitled to any OBC relaxation/reservation and must indicate their category as General.
  • Benefit of reservation under the EWS category requires an Income and Asset Certificate for financial year 2025-26, valid for 2026-27, issued by a Competent Authority on the Government of India format.

The total starting emoluments of a Clerical Cadre employee posted at a Metro like Mumbai will be around Rs. 46,000 per month, inclusive of Dearness Allowance, other allowances at the current rate, and two additional increments for newly recruited graduate Junior Associates. Allowances may vary depending on the place of posting. Selected candidates will be eligible for reimbursement of various perquisites, provident fund, pension under the New Pension Scheme (Defined Contribution Benefit), medical, leave-fare, and other facilities as per Bank instructions issued from time to time.

How to Apply for SBI Junior Associate Recruitment 2026

  2. Scroll down and click on the relevant advertisement, then download and carefully read Advertisement No. CRPD/CR/2026-27/17.
  3. Register online under "Recruitment of Junior Associates 2026", providing your details in one sitting or saving and resuming (available up to three times before final submission).
  4. Upload your scanned photograph, signature, left-hand thumb impression, and hand-written declaration as per the specified guidelines, and capture a live photograph via webcam or mobile phone.
  5. Pay the requisite application fee online through debit card, credit card, or Internet Banking (fee is Nil for SC/ST/PwBD/XS/DXS, and ₹750 for General/OBC/EWS candidates).
  6. Review your application carefully before final submission - no corrections or edits are allowed after final submission.
  7. Submit the application before the last date, 31.08.2026, and take a printout of the system-generated application form for your own record (this printout is not to be sent to SBI).

SBI Junior Associate Recruitment 2026 Important Instructions

  • Not more than one application should be submitted by a candidate. In case of multiple applications, only the last valid (completed) application will be retained, and the fee paid for other registrations will be forfeited.
  • Request for change or correction of any particulars, including category, once the application is submitted, will not be entertained under any circumstances.
  • Candidates are advised to apply well before the closing date to avoid last-minute connectivity issues; SBI will not be responsible for failure to submit an application due to heavy website traffic or reasons beyond its control.
  • Mobile phones, pagers, smart watches, calculators, or any other communication/electronic devices are not allowed inside the examination premises.
  • The Bank may capture thumb impressions or IRIS scans at various stages for biometric verification; any inconsistency may lead to rejection of candidature.
  • Candidates found using unfair means, impersonation, or misbehaviour during the examination may be disqualified, debarred from future Bank examinations, and held liable for criminal prosecution.
  • Canvassing in any form will lead to disqualification.
  • No hard copy of the call letter (Preliminary/Main) or the "Acquaint Yourself" booklet will be sent by post; candidates must download these from the Bank's website.
  • Appointment of selected candidates is subject to being declared medically fit and satisfactory completion of Know Your Employee (KYE) formalities, as well as the Bank's service and conduct rules.
  • Any legal proceedings relating to this advertisement or an application can only be instituted in Mumbai; courts, tribunals, and forums at Mumbai alone have jurisdiction.
  • The role requires flair for marketing and customer calls, banking, advisory, and cross-selling duties, both inside and outside Bank premises, with possible extensive outdoor travel and flexible working hours/shifts.
  • Decisions of the Bank in all matters regarding eligibility, conduct of tests, and selection are final and binding on all candidates; no representation or correspondence will be entertained.
  • The Bank reserves the right to cancel the recruitment process entirely at any stage.
  • State Bank of India does not endorse, authorize, or associate with any external coaching platform, consultancy, individual, or digital channel claiming to provide guaranteed selection or insider guidance. Candidates must rely solely on information available on SBI's official career portal.

Indian Overseas Bank (IOB) has released the IOB Local Bank Officer (LBO) Recruitment 2026-27 notification (Advt. No. HRDD/RECT/02/2026-27, dated 07.08.2026) for 250 vacancies in the JMGS-I (Junior Management Grade Scale I) cadre. Eligible candidates who hold a graduate degree in any discipline can apply online from 8 August 2026 to 24 August 2026 through the official website www.iob.bank.in. Selection is through an Online Examination, a Language Proficiency Test (where applicable), and a Personal Interview. Selected candidates will be posted only within the state for which they apply, for the first 12 years of service or until promotion to SMGS-IV, whichever is earlier.

Indian Overseas Bank LBO Recruitment 2026 Notification PDF

IOB Local Bank Officer Eligibility Criteria 2026-27

Candidates can apply for the vacancy of only one state and must fulfil the eligibility criteria specified for that state, including the mandatory local language proficiency.

Nationality/Citizenship

A candidate must be a citizen of India, or a subject of Nepal or Bhutan, or a Tibetan refugee who came to India before 1 January 1962 with the intention of settling permanently, or a person of Indian origin who has migrated from Pakistan, Burma, Sri Lanka, East African countries (Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Zambia, Malawi, Zaire, Ethiopia) or Vietnam with the intention of settling permanently in India, subject to the required eligibility certificate from the Government of India.

IOB LBO Educational Qualification

Candidates must hold a Degree (Graduation) in any discipline from a recognized university or an equivalent qualification recognized by the Central Government. Candidates must possess a valid mark-sheet/degree certificate showing they are a graduate on the day they register, and must indicate their graduation percentage while registering online.

IOB Local Bank Officer Selection Process 2026-27

Selection is made through an Online Examination, followed by a Language Proficiency Test (LPT) for candidates who have not studied the applied state's local language in Std. X or Std. XII, and a Personal Interview.

Online Examination Structure

Section No. of Questions Maximum Marks Medium Duration
Reasoning and Computer Aptitude 30 60 English & Hindi 60 minutes
General/Economy/Banking Awareness 40 40 English & Hindi 30 minutes
Data Analysis and Interpretation 30 60 English & Hindi 60 minutes
English Knowledge 40 40 English 30 minutes
Total 140 200 - 3 hours

There is a penalty of 0.25 marks for each wrong answer, with no penalty for unattempted questions. There is no sectional cut-off, but the minimum qualifying aggregate is 30% for reserved category candidates and 35% for unreserved candidates.

Language Proficiency Test (LPT)

Candidates shortlisted for the Personal Interview who have not studied the applied state's local language in Std. X or Std. XII must qualify an LPT before the interview. Candidates who fail the LPT will not proceed further in the selection process.

Personal Interview

The Personal Interview carries 100 marks. The minimum qualifying marks are 45% for reserved category candidates and 50% for unreserved candidates.

Final Selection

The weightage of Online Examination and Personal Interview is in the ratio of 80:20. The minimum aggregate score (Online Exam + Interview) required is 30% for reserved categories and 35% for unreserved category candidates. The final merit list is prepared state-wise and category-wise.

Probation and Bond

Selected candidates will be on probation for 2 years of active service from the date of joining. They must execute a Financial Service Indemnity Bond of ₹2,00,000 for rendering a minimum of 3 years of service.

Documents Required at Personal Interview

  • Printout of the valid Personal Interview call letter
  • Printout of the system-generated online application form
  • Proof of date of birth (Birth Certificate or Std. X certificate with DOB)
  • Proof of language proficiency (Std. X/XII certificate with subjects passed)
  • Photo ID proof (Passport/Aadhaar/e-Aadhaar/PAN/Driving Licence/Voter's Card)
  • Mark sheets and certificates for educational qualification
  • Work experience documents (Experience Certificate, Appointment/Relieving Letters, Salary Slips), where applicable
  • Caste certificate (SC/ST/OBC) or Income and Asset Certificate (EWS), where applicable
  • Disability certificate in the prescribed format, for PwBD candidates
  • No Objection Certificate, for candidates already working in Government/PSU/Bank roles

How to Apply for IOB Local Bank Officer Recruitment 2026-27

  1. Visit the official IOB website, www.iob.bank.in, and open the "Careers" page.
  2. Click on "Recruitment of Local Bank Officers – 2026-27" and select the post to apply.
  3. Click "Click here to Register Online" and complete first-time registration.
  4. Note the system-generated Registration Number and Password sent by email/SMS.
  5. Log in and upload photograph, signature, left thumb impression and handwritten declaration as per the specified format.
  6. Fill in all required details in the online application form carefully and accurately.
  7. Pay the applicable application fee/intimation charges online.
  8. Click "Complete Registration" and take a printout of the submitted application form and fee e-receipt for future reference.

Applications can be submitted only online from 08.08.2026 to 24.08.2026. No other mode of application is accepted, and applications once submitted cannot be withdrawn.

Important Instructions

  • Candidates can apply for only one state; a candidate applying for one state's vacancy is not eligible to apply for any other state.
  • Selected candidates will be posted within the applied state for the first 12 years of service or until promotion to SMGS-IV, whichever is earlier.
  • Application Fee/Intimation charges, once paid, are non-refundable and cannot be adjusted against any other recruitment process.
  • If multiple applications are submitted for the same state, only the last submitted application will be considered.
  • Ration Card and Learner's Driving Licence are not accepted as valid photo ID proof.
  • Request for change of examination centre, Personal Interview date, or centre will not be entertained.
  • Candidates working in Government/Quasi-Government/PSU roles must produce a No Objection Certificate at the time of Personal Interview.

IOB LBO Examination Centres

The online examination will be conducted at various centres across India, including Chennai, Madurai, Coimbatore, Tiruchirappalli in Tamil Nadu; Bengaluru, Hubli-Dharwad, Mysuru in Karnataka; Mumbai/Thane/Navi Mumbai, Pune, Nagpur in Maharashtra; and Ahmedabad/Gandhinagar, Surat, Rajkot in Gujarat, among other centres nationwide. The Bank reserves the right to add, delete, or reassign examination centres based on response and administrative feasibility.

SBI Junior Associate Exam Pattern 2026

The selection process has three stages: Preliminary Examination, Main Examination, and (where applicable) a Local Language Proficiency Test. Both online tests carry negative marking of 1/4th mark for every wrong answer.

Phase I: Preliminary Examination Pattern

The Prelims is an objective test of 100 marks and 1 hour total duration, split into three separately timed sections. There is no sectional cut-off, but the Bank shortlists candidates for Mains based on aggregate marks (approximately 10 times the number of vacancies per category, subject to availability).

Total 100 100 1 Hour

Phase II: Main Examination Pattern

The Main Exam is an objective test of 200 marks over 2 hours 40 minutes, with four separately timed sections. Only the aggregate marks obtained in the Main Examination are used to prepare the final merit list Prelims marks are not added at this stage.

Phase III: Local Language Proficiency Test (LLPT)

Provisionally selected candidates who have not studied the specified local language of the applied state in Class 10 or 12 must appear for the LLPT after Main Exam qualification but before joining. SBI Junior Associate Syllabus 2026 (Section-wise Guide)

The notification does not release a detailed, topic-wise syllabus it only names the test sections shown above. Based on the officially named sections, the following are the broad areas typically covered under each section for this kind of clerical-cadre banking exam. Treat this as a general study guide, not an official syllabus document.

Prelims Sections

  • English Language: Reading comprehension, cloze test, para jumbles, error detection, fill in the blanks, vocabulary-based questions.
  • Numerical Ability: Simplification, number series, quadratic equations, data interpretation, arithmetic problems (percentage, profit & loss, average, ratio, time & work, simple/compound interest).
  • Reasoning Ability: Puzzles, seating arrangement, syllogism, inequality, coding-decoding, blood relations, direction sense, alphanumeric series.

Mains Sections

  • General/Financial Awareness: Current affairs, banking and financial awareness, static general knowledge.
  • General English: Comprehension, grammar, vocabulary, sentence correction, and para-based questions at a slightly higher difficulty than Prelims.
  • Quantitative Aptitude: Data interpretation, data sufficiency, arithmetic word problems, number series, simplification/approximation.
  • Reasoning Ability & Computer Aptitude: Advanced puzzles and seating arrangement, logical reasoning, plus basic computer knowledge (fundamentals, MS Office, internet, and banking-related computer terms).

The mandatory educational qualification and minimum post-qualification experience required for each post are summarised in the table below. Candidates should refer to the official notification for complete details of preferred qualifications and certifications.

Post Mandatory Qualification Minimum Experience
Manager – Digital Product B.E./B.Tech in IT/Computer Science/Electronics & Communication Engineering 3 years in project management of digital/IT products in Bank, BFSI, FinTech or Card Networks
Senior Manager – Digital Product B.E./B.Tech in CS/Computer Applications/IT/Electronics/Telecom/E&C/E&I, or MCA 6 years in project management of digital/IT products in Bank, BFSI, FinTech or Card Networks

Manager – Security Graduate in any discipline Officer with minimum 5 years Commissioned Service in Army/Navy/Air Force, OR Police officer not below Deputy Superintendent of Police rank with 5 years as Class-I Gazetted Officer, OR rank equivalent to/above Assistant Commandant with 5 years as Class-I Gazetted Officer in Paramilitary Forces
Chief Manager – Data Scientist B.E./B.Tech/M.E./M.Tech (CS/IT/Electronics & Telecom/E&C) or B.Sc/M.Sc (CS/IT/Data Science) or BCA/MCA or Graduation in Data Science/Statistics/Applied Mathematics 10 years in IT, of which 8 years in Data Science
Senior Manager – Data Scientist Same qualification stream as Chief Manager – Data Scientist 6 years in IT, of which 5 years in Data Science/Data Analytics
Senior Manager – Data Profiling B.Sc (IT/CS) or BE/B.Tech (CS/IT/E&Telecom/E&C) or BCA/MCA 6 years in IT, of which 5 years in SQL/PL-SQL or Impala/Hive Query and Qlik Development
Senior Manager – DQ Analyst Graduation (CS/Information Systems/Statistics/Data Science/Mathematics or related quantitative field) or M.Sc (Data Science) or MBA (with analytics) 6 years in IT, of which 5 years as a Data Quality Analyst
Senior Manager – BI and Dashboard Development B.E./B.Tech (CS/IT/E&C/E&Telecom) or MCA or M.Sc (IT/CS) 6 years in IT, of which 5 years in SQL/PL-SQL or Impala/Hive Query
Manager – Taxation / Manager – Accounts Chartered Accountant / ICWA 2 years total in BFSI, of which 1 year preferably in Accounts & Taxation
Senior Manager – Taxation / Senior Manager – Accounts Chartered Accountant / ICWA 5 years total in BFSI, of which 2 years preferably in Accounts & Taxation
Chief Manager – Investor Relations Graduation in Economics or Commerce 8 years in Banking Sector or reputed Brokerage Firms, of which 3 years in Investor Relations/Corporate Communication/Research

Educational qualifications must be from a University/Institute/Board recognised by the Government of India or approved regulatory bodies. Post-qualification experience of less than six months in any organisation as on 01.08.2026 will not be considered for eligibility, and experience in the Clerical cadre is not counted.

BoB Recruitment 2026 Age Limit

The minimum and maximum age limits vary by post and grade, and are calculated as on 01.08.2026.

BoB Professionals Recruitment 2026 Salary

Selected candidates will draw pay as per the grade/scale applicable to their post, governed by the industry-level bipartite settlement and Joint Note for bank officers, in addition to allowances and benefits as per the Bank's policies.

The application fee is non-refundable and must be paid online through Debit Card, Credit Card, Internet Banking, or UPI. The fee is payable irrespective of whether an online test is conducted or whether the candidate is shortlisted for interview.

BoB Professionals Recruitment 2026 Selection Process

The selection process for BoB Recruitment 2026 may comprise Application Scrutiny, an Online Test, a Psychometric Test, and/or a Group Discussion and Personal Interview, as decided by the Bank for each post.

  • Online Test (if conducted): Tentative structure includes Reasoning (25 questions/25 marks), English Language (25 questions/25 marks), Quantitative Aptitude (25 questions/25 marks), and Professional Knowledge (75 questions/150 marks), for a total of 150 questions/225 marks in 150 minutes. Reasoning, English Language, and Quantitative Aptitude sections are qualifying in nature; only Professional Knowledge marks count toward the final result. There is a penalty of 0.25 marks for each wrong answer.
  • Psychometric Test/Personal Interview (PI): Conducted to assess personality, communication, problem-solving ability, efficiency, and willingness to work in any part of the country. The minimum qualifying marks for PI are 60% for General & EWS category and 55% for other reserved categories.
  • Final Selection: Based on combined scores from the Online Test and/or PI, subject to vacancies available under the respective category.

BoB Professionals Recruitment 2026 Documents Required

Candidates must produce the following original documents, along with self-attested photocopies, at the time of interview or any subsequent stage of selection:

  • Printout of the valid Interview Call Letter
  • System-generated printout of the online application form
  • Proof of Date of Birth (birth certificate or SSLC/Std. X marksheet)
  • Photo identity proof (PAN Card/Passport/Driving Licence/Voter's Card/Bank Passbook with photo/Aadhaar card, etc.)
  • Individual semester/year-wise mark sheets and final degree/diploma certificate
  • Caste certificate (for SC/ST/OBC candidates, in the prescribed format)
  • OBC non-creamy layer certificate (valid as on the date of interview)
  • Disability certificate in the prescribed format (for PwBD candidates)
  • Service/Discharge Book and pension payment order (for Ex-servicemen candidates)
  • No Objection Certificate from current employer (for candidates serving in Government/Quasi-Government/PSU/Bank)
  • Documents supporting work experience (appointment letter, salary slips, relieving letter, etc.)
  • Any other relevant document in support of eligibility

How to Apply for BoB Professionals Recruitment 2026

  1. Visit the official Bank of Baroda website at www.bankofbaroda.bank.in and go to the Career section → Current Opportunities.
  2. Register online using a valid personal email ID and mobile number, which must be kept active till completion of the recruitment process.
  3. Fill in the online application form carefully, upload a scanned photograph, signature, and supporting documents such as Date of Birth proof, qualification certificates, experience letters, and category certificates, as per the specifications given in the notification.
  4. Verify all details before submitting, since no changes are permitted after clicking the Submit button.
  5. Pay the applicable application fee online through Debit Card, Credit Card, Internet Banking, or UPI.
  6. On successful payment, download and retain a printout of the e-receipt and the completed application form for future reference.

BoB Professionals Recruitment 2026 Important Instructions

  • Only candidates willing to serve anywhere in India should apply, as selected candidates will be posted at the Bank's absolute discretion.
  • Selected candidates will be on probation for a period of 12 months.
  • Candidates selected for JMG/S-I posts must execute a service bond to serve for a minimum of 3 years or pay an amount equivalent to three months' gross salary (not exceeding Rs. 2 lakh) if they leave before completing three years.
  • Candidates selected for MMG/S-II, MMG/S-III, and SMG/S-IV posts must execute a similar service bond, with the payable amount not exceeding Rs. 3 lakh.
  • Change of category is not permitted at any stage after registration of the online application.
  • There is no reservation for Ex-servicemen in the Officers' Cadre.
  • The number of vacancies, including reserved vacancies, is provisional and may vary according to the Bank's actual requirement.
  • Not more than one application should be submitted by a candidate; in case of multiple applications, only the latest valid (completed) application will be retained.

The Railway Recruitment Board (RRB) conducts the RRB JE Exam to select candidates for Junior Engineer (JE), Depot Material Superintendent (DMS), and Chemical & Metallurgical Assistant (CMA) posts across Indian Railways. The RRB JE 2026 recruitment cycle (CEN 04/2026) was announced in August 2026, with the online application window opening on 14 August 2026. Knowing the RRB JE Syllabus 2026 and exam pattern together is essential before starting preparation, as the exam is conducted in two stages (CBT 1 and CBT 2) that test different subjects and difficulty levels. This article covers the subject-wise syllabus, exam pattern, selection process, and preparation tips for RRB JE.

RRB JE Syllabus and Exam Pattern 2026 - Overview

Feature Details
Conducting Body Railway Recruitment Board (RRB)
Exam Name RRB JE Exam
Posts Junior Engineer (JE), Depot Material Superintendent (DMS), Chemical & Metallurgical Assistant (CMA)
Recruitment Cycle CEN 04/2026 (application window opened 14 August 2026)
Selection Stages CBT 1, CBT 2, Document Verification, Medical Examination
Total Questions CBT 1 – 100; CBT 2 – 150
Total Marks CBT 1 – 100; CBT 2 – 150
Duration CBT 1 – 90 minutes; CBT 2 – 120 minutes
Marking Scheme 1 mark per correct answer
Negative Marking 1/3 mark deducted per wrong answer
Official Website https://rrbcdg.gov.in/

RRB JE Selection Process 2026

Candidates are selected through the following stages, in order:

  1. First Stage CBT (CBT 1): A screening-level test covering Mathematics, General Intelligence & Reasoning, General Awareness, and General Science. Only candidates who clear CBT 1 (based on RRB's normalization and cut-off process) move to CBT 2.
  2. Second Stage CBT (CBT 2): A more technical test covering General Awareness, Physics & Chemistry, Basics of Computer Applications, Basics of Environment & Pollution Control, and Technical Abilities specific to the candidate's engineering discipline. Final merit is based on CBT 2 performance.
  3. Document Verification (DV): Shortlisted candidates, based on CBT 2 merit and category-wise vacancies, are called to verify educational certificates, category certificates, and other documents.
  4. Medical Examination (ME): Candidates who clear DV undergo a medical fitness test as per the medical standards prescribed for the specific post.

Note: CBT 1 is only a qualifying/screening stage and its marks are not typically counted toward final merit, which is based on CBT 2. This is consistent with the pattern description in the reference sources; candidates should confirm the exact merit-weightage rule in the official notification.

Also Read: RRB JE 04/2026 Recruitment 2026 Notification

RRB JE Exam Pattern 2026

RRB JE CBT 1 Exam Pattern

Subject No. of Questions Marks
Mathematics 30 30
General Intelligence & Reasoning 25 25
General Awareness 15 15
General Science 30 30
Total 100 100

CBT 1 consists of 100 objective-type MCQs, to be completed in 90 minutes. Each correct answer carries 1 mark, and 1/3 mark is deducted for every wrong answer.

RRB JE CBT 2 Exam Pattern

Subject No. of Questions Marks
General Awareness 15 15
Physics & Chemistry 15 15
Basics of Computer Applications 10 10
Basics of Environment & Pollution Control 10 10
Technical Abilities (branch-specific) 100 100
Total 150 150

CBT 2 consists of 150 objective-type MCQs, to be completed in 120 minutes (2 hours), with the same marking scheme of 1 mark per correct answer and 1/3 mark negative marking per wrong answer. Since Technical Abilities alone accounts for 100 of the 150 marks in CBT 2, it carries the largest share of this stage this is a direct read of the marks distribution above, not a separate weightage claim from any source.

RRB JE Syllabus 2026

The RRB JE Syllabus is divided into the CBT 1 syllabus (screening-level, common to all candidates) and the CBT 2 syllabus (common sections plus a Technical Abilities section specific to the candidate's engineering branch). The detailed topic-wise breakdown is given below.

1. Mathematics (CBT 1)

  • Number systems
  • BODMAS
  • Decimals
  • Fractions
  • LCM and HCF
  • Ratio and Proportion
  • Percentages
  • Mensuration
  • Time and Work
  • Time and Distance
  • Simple and Compound Interest
  • Profit and Loss
  • Algebra
  • Geometry
  • Trigonometry
  • Elementary Statistics
  • Square Root
  • Age Calculations
  • Calendar & Clock
  • Pipes & Cistern

2. General Intelligence and Reasoning (CBT 1)

  • Analogies
  • Alphabetical and Number Series
  • Coding and Decoding
  • Mathematical operations
  • Relationships
  • Syllogism
  • Jumbling
  • Venn Diagram
  • Data Interpretation and Sufficiency
  • Conclusions and Decision-Making
  • Similarities and Differences
  • Analytical reasoning
  • Classification
  • Directions
  • Statement – Arguments and Assumptions

3. General Awareness (CBT 1 and CBT 2 – common)

  • Current affairs
  • Indian Geography
  • Culture and history of India, including the freedom struggle
  • Indian Polity and Constitution
  • Indian Economy
  • Environmental issues concerning India and the world, sports, and general scientific and technological developments

4. General Science (CBT 1)

  • Physics, Chemistry, and Life Sciences up to 10th standard CBSE syllabus

5. Physics and Chemistry (CBT 2)

Questions are set from 12th-standard-level Physics and Chemistry, carrying 15 questions in CBT 2.

6. Basics of Computer Applications (CBT 2)

  • Computers and their architecture
  • Input & Output devices
  • MS Office
  • Storage devices
  • Operating Systems
  • Internet and Email
  • Websites & Web Browsers
  • Networking
  • Computer Virus

7. Basics of Environment and Pollution Control (CBT 2)

  • Basics of Environment
  • Adverse effects of environmental pollution
  • Pollution control strategies
  • Types of pollution
  • Waste Management
  • Global warming
  • Acid rain
  • Ozone depletion

8. Technical Abilities (CBT 2 – branch-specific)

This section carries 100 of the 150 marks in CBT 2 and is based on the engineering branch/discipline the candidate has applied for. The branch-wise syllabus is given below.

(A) Civil & Allied Engineering

Topic Sub-topics
Engineering Mechanics Force, moment, force systems, equilibrium, friction, centroid, centre of gravity, simple machines
Building Construction Substructure and superstructure components; load-bearing, framed, and composite structures
Building Materials Masonry materials, timber, glass, plastic, aluminum, steel, bitumen, PVC, CPVC, PPF
Substructure Construction Job layout, earthwork, foundation types, dewatering, coffer dams, bearing capacity
Superstructure Construction Masonry types, cavity walls, doors/windows, stairs, lifts, escalators, scaffolding, shoring
Building Finishes Floor finishes, wall plastering/pointing/painting, roofing materials including RCC
Building Maintenance Cracks and repairs (grouting, guniting, epoxy), settlement causes/remedies, re-baring
Building Drawing Conventions, planning principles, byelaws, plan/elevation/section drawings, perspective drawing
Concrete Technology Cement grades, aggregates, mix design, testing, quality control, admixtures, special concretes
Surveying Chain survey, compass survey, leveling, contouring, plane table, theodolite, tacheometry, curves, aerial survey, remote sensing
Computer-Aided Design CAD software (AutoCAD, Auto Civil, 3D Max), plan/elevation/section generation, 3D views
Geotechnical Engineering Soil properties, permeability, seepage, shear strength, bearing capacity, compaction, site investigation
Hydraulics Fluid properties, hydrostatic pressure, pipe flow, open channel flow, flow-measuring devices, hydraulic machines
Irrigation Engineering Hydrology, reservoir planning, percolation tanks, diversion headworks
Mechanics of Structures Stress, strain, shear force, bending moment, moment of inertia, trusses, strain energy
Theory of Structures Direct and bending stresses, slope/deflection, fixed and continuous beams, moment distribution, columns
Design of Concrete Structures Working stress and limit state methods, reinforced sections, shear, bond, development length, T-beams, footings
Design of Steel Structures Sections, steel grades, IS codes, connections, tension/compression members, trusses, beams, columns
Transportation Engineering Railway engineering, bridge engineering, tunnel engineering
Highway Engineering Road investigation, geometric design, pavement construction, traffic engineering, drainage, maintenance
Environmental Engineering Pollution control, water supply, sewage, solid waste management, sanitation, plumbing
Advanced Construction Techniques Fibers, plastics, advanced concreting, formwork, prefabrication, earth-moving machinery
Estimating and Costing Approximate and detailed estimates, measurement modes, rate analysis
Contracts and Accounts Types of engineering contracts, tender documents, payment, specifications

(B) Electrical & Allied Engineering

Topic Sub-topics
Basic Concepts Resistance, inductance, capacitance, current, voltage, power, energy, units
Circuit Law Kirchhoff's laws, network theorems
Magnetic Circuit Flux, mmf, reluctance, magnetic materials, electromagnetic induction, self/mutual induction
AC Fundamentals Instantaneous/peak/RMS/average values, sinusoidal waveforms, series/parallel AC circuits, resonance, poly-phase systems, star/delta connection
Measurement and Instruments Power/energy measurement, wattmeter methods, frequency/phase measurement, ammeters, voltmeters, multimeters, Megger, AC bridges, CRO, CT, PT
Electrical Machines DC machines, transformers (construction, equivalent circuit, tests, efficiency), 3-phase induction motors, single-phase motors
Synchronous Machines EMF generation, armature reaction, voltage regulation, parallel operation, synchronizing
Generation, Transmission & Distribution Power stations, load factor, tariffs, faults, switchgear, protection, Buchholz relay, Merz-Price system, lightning arresters, cables
Estimation and Costing Lighting scheme estimation, electric installation, IE rules, earthing practices
Utilization of Electrical Energy Illumination, electric heating, welding, electroplating, electric drives and motors
Basic Electronics Diodes, transistors (BJT, JFET), simple circuits using these devices

(C) Electronics & Telecommunication Engineering

Topic Sub-topics
Electronic Components & Materials Conductors, semiconductors, insulators, magnetic materials, cells, batteries, relays, switches, MCBs, connectors
Electronic Devices and Circuits PN junction diodes, thyristors, transistors, amplifiers, oscillators, multivibrators, counters, rectifiers, inverters, UPS
Digital Electronics Number systems, binary codes, Boolean algebra, logic gates, combinational/sequential circuits, A/D and D/A converters, memories
Linear Integrated Circuit Operational amplifiers, linear/non-linear applications, voltage regulators, timers, phase-locked loops
Microprocessor and Microcontroller 8085 microprocessor, assembly language programming, peripherals, microcontrollers
Electronic Measurements Measuring systems, range extension, CRO, LCD/LED panels, transducers
Communication Engineering Modulation, multiplexing, wave propagation, transmission lines, OFC, public address systems, radar, satellite communication
Data Communication and Network Hardware/interface, LAN/WAN, networking devices, internetworking
Computer Programming C and C++ fundamentals, operators, control statements, functions, arrays, strings, pointers, data structures, DBMS
Basic Electrical Engineering DC circuits, AC fundamentals, magnetic/thermal/chemical effects of current, earthing

(D) Mechanical & Allied Engineering

Topic Sub-topics
Engineering Mechanics Resolution of forces, equilibrium, friction, moment of inertia, Newton's laws, projectile motion, D'Alembert's principle
Material Science Mechanical properties of materials, classification of steels, heat treatment processes
Strength of Materials Stress, strain, factor of safety, thermal stresses, shear force/bending moment diagrams, torsion
Machining Lathe operations, cutting tools, shaper, slotter, planer, milling, gear manufacture
Welding Arc and gas welding, soldering, brazing, MIG/TIG welding, welding defects
Grinding & Finishing Process Metal removal principles, abrasives, grinding machines, honing, lapping, electroplating
Metrology Linear/angle measurement, comparators, surface roughness measurement, interferometry
Fluid Mechanics & Hydraulic Machinery Fluid properties, Bernoulli's equation, venturimeters, pitot tubes, centrifugal pumps

Note: The Mechanical branch syllabus, per the reference sources, also includes Industrial Management and Thermal Engineering topics (thermodynamics laws, IC engines, refrigeration cycles) that are not repeated in the table above for brevity refer to the official notification for the complete branch syllabus.

(E) Computer Science & Information Technology

Topic Sub-topics
PC Software MS Windows, MS Word, MS Excel, MS PowerPoint
Computer Fundamentals Evolution of computers, hardware & software, Internet
C Language Structure, loops, control statements, arrays, pointers, functions, structures, unions, files
Computer Organisation Number systems, logic gates, flip-flops, Boolean algebra, DMA, instruction sets
Data Structures using C++ OOP concepts, stacks, queues, linked lists, searching and sorting algorithms
DBMS Fundamentals Data models, RDBMS, relational algebra, SQL, PL/SQL, cursors, triggers
Operating Systems (Linux) Unix/Linux architecture, file system, commands, system administration
Web Technologies Internet/Intranet, LAN, routers, HTML basics, web servers, browsers, security
Data and Network Communication OSI model, TCP/IP, transmission media, error detection/correction, Ethernet
Java Programming JVM, data types, classes, objects, inheritance, threads, applets
Software Engineering Life cycle models, requirements analysis, design principles, testing strategies, project management

(F) Printing Technology

Covers printing systems, printing materials, flexo/gravure/screen printing, printing finishing processes, image processing, design & advertising in print media, sheet-fed and web offset machines, publishing software, colour separation, plate-making methods, and printer's accounting per the branch-wise syllabus in the reference sources. Refer to the official notification for the full topic list, as this branch's syllabus is extensive.

(G) Chemical & Metallurgical Assistant (CMA)

The CMA technical syllabus covers general science topics at an intermediate level, including:

  • Measurements, units, dimensions, and errors in measurement
  • Light: reflection, refraction, interference, diffraction, polarization
  • Heat: transmission, expansion, calorimetry, latent heat
  • Sound: propagation, characteristics, resonance, Doppler effect
  • Mechanics: motion, friction, Newton's laws, momentum, gravitation
  • Magnetism and Electricity & Electromagnetism
  • Modern Physics: atomic models, radioactivity, nuclear reactions
  • Electronics and Communications: semiconductors, diodes, transistors, logic gates
  • Matter, Chemical Reactions, Acids/Bases/Salts
  • Atomic Structure and Periodic Classification of Elements
  • Chemical Bonding, Carbon and its Compounds
  • Environmental Chemistry and Metallurgy

How to Prepare for RRB JE Exam 2026

  1. Start with the syllabus, not question banks. Map out CBT 1 subjects first since it's the qualifying stage, then move to your specific Technical Abilities branch for CBT 2.
  2. Build a subject-wise timetable. Since Technical Abilities alone carries 100 of 150 marks in CBT 2, allocate proportionally more study time to your branch subjects than to General Awareness or Computer Basics.
  3. Use RRB JE previous year question papers (PYQs). This helps you understand question difficulty and recurring topic patterns across CBT 1 and CBT 2.
  4. Take sectional mock tests as you finish each subject. Don't wait until the full syllabus is done test topic-wise to catch weak areas early.
  5. Revise General Science and General Awareness weekly. These sections change least in preparation strategy but need regular touchpoints, unlike technical subjects that need deep, one-time study.
  6. Practice negative-marking-aware attempts in mocks. With 1/3 mark deducted per wrong answer, build the habit of skipping low-confidence questions during timed practice.

Other Eligibility Conditions

  • Applicants must be resident and/or registered with a local Employment Exchange within Tamil Nadu, with registration date not beyond the application's last date, except wards of Railway employees.
  • Wards of Railway employees must submit the Railway employee's Identity Card/Service Certificate (attested by a Gazetted Officer), along with UMID card and PPO copy as proof.
  • Vacancies for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities are reserved trade-wise, subject to permissible disability categories and a minimum of 40% relevant disability; a disability certificate from the Central/State Government is required to claim this benefit.

ICF Act Apprentice Age Limit

Age will be reckoned as on 7 September 2026.

  • ITI candidates: must have completed 15 years and not completed 24 years of age.
  • Non-ITI candidates: must have completed 15 years and not completed 22 years of age.
  • Upper age relaxation: 5 years for SC/ST candidates, 3 years for OBC candidates.
  • Upper age relaxation for Persons with Disability: 10 years.
  • SC/ST candidates must produce a caste certificate, and OBC candidates must produce an OBC Non-Creamy Layer certificate, at the time of Document Verification.

Candidates are advised to check whether they satisfy the prescribed age limit before applying. Use our online Age Calculator to calculate your exact age instantly.

ICF Act Apprentice Application Fee

  • A processing fee of ₹100 plus applicable service charges (non-refundable) must be paid online.
  • No application fee is required for SC, ST, PwBD, and Women candidates.
  • No request for refund of fee once remitted will be entertained under any circumstances.
  • After successful payment (for candidates other than SC/ST/PwBD/Women), a unique Transaction ID starting with "DU" is sent to the registered mobile number and should be preserved for future reference.

ICF Act Apprentice Selection Process

  • The merit list is prepared based on marks obtained in Std X. For COVID-pass candidates in Std X, proof of the IX std mark sheet or X std half-yearly mark sheet duly signed by the Principal will be considered.
  • If two candidates have equal marks, the candidate with older age is preferred; if dates of birth are also the same, the candidate who passed Std X earlier is considered first.
  • Freshers exercise trade options, and trades are allotted based on merit order and vacancy availability; once allotted, requests for change of trade are not entertained. Candidates selected against benchmark disabilities are allotted only the trade permissible to them.
  • Ex-ITI candidates are trained in the trade for which they hold an ITI certificate.
  • Selected candidates must be physically fit as per the Apprentices Act, 1961 and Apprentices Rules, and must produce a Medical Certificate from a Government-authorised doctor (not below the rank of Assistant Surgeon) at Document Verification.
  • Selected candidates must execute a contract of apprenticeship; if a candidate is a minor, their guardian executes the contract as per the guidelines of the Regional Director of Apprenticeship Training, Guindy, Chennai.
  • Original Transfer Certificate for the qualifying examination (Std X/XII/ITI) must be produced during document verification.

How to Apply for ICF Act Apprentice Recruitment 2026

  1. Visit the ICF web portal at pb.icf.gov.in.
  2. Read the notification thoroughly before filling the online application form.
  3. Keep all relevant documents/certificates and a recent passport-size photograph (maximum 200 KB, jpg/jpeg format) ready before starting the form.
  4. Fill in the required details and submit the application; a system-generated registration number will be issued as the individual Registration ID, with the date of birth (in ddmmyyyy format) as the password for the acknowledgement.
  5. Pay the processing fee of ₹100 plus applicable service charges online (not applicable for SC/ST/PwBD/Women candidates).
  6. Check all details carefully before clicking the submit button.
  7. Generate and print the system acknowledgement after final submission; this printout is required at the time of Document Verification.

Candidates are not required to send any documents or the application form to ICF through Post, e-mail, FAX, or by hand. All communication from ICF will be sent only by SMS (from "PBICF") or email to the mobile number and e-mail ID mentioned in the application, so candidates should maintain the same contact details until selection is complete.

Also Read: RRB JE 04/2026 Recruitment 2026 Notification Out - Apply Online for 4098 Junior Engineer Posts

ICF Act Apprentice Important Instructions

  • This notification is purely for apprenticeship training and not for employment; no employment is guaranteed to apprentices on completion of training.
  • Imparting training at ICF confers no right to absorption in Railways after successful completion, as per the Apprenticeship Rules, 1991.
  • Canvassing in any form will disqualify the candidature, and no correspondence will be entertained in this regard.
  • If any declaration furnished by a candidate is found false, they will be disqualified or terminated at any stage of training without notice.
  • Accommodation must be arranged at the candidate's own cost; ICF will not provide food or accommodation.
  • Candidates selected for training will not be allowed to withdraw except for reasons beyond their control; those who wilfully remain absent are liable to refund the full training cost and stipend paid.
  • For clarifications, candidates may use the helpdesk at pb.icf.gov.in/act2026_cc/helpdesk_entry.php.

A final answer key is the last, legally binding version of the answer key. RSSB releases it only after reviewing every objection candidates raised against the earlier provisional answer key.   2. Open the Recruitment Portal from your dashboard.
  3. Select "Question Objection" for the Sr. Teacher (Sec. Edu.) Comp. Exam 2025.
  4. Choose the subject, paper, and question number as per the Model Question Paper (not your individual set order).
  5. Upload authentic supporting proof standard reference books such as NCERT texts or Board of Secondary Education Rajasthan textbooks; coaching notes or blog links are not accepted.
  6. Pay the objection fee (Rs. 100 per question in earlier batches) via e-Mitra, net banking, or card.
  7. Submit and download the acknowledgement receipt.

About UPSC Indian Statistical Service (ISS) Examination 2026

The ISS Examination is one of the premier competitive exams conducted by UPSC to recruit officers for Group A and Group B posts in the Indian Statistical Service. Understanding the exam structure helps candidates correctly interpret the provisional answer key.

The Indian Statistical Service (ISS) Examination is conducted annually by the Union Public Service Commission to fill vacancies in the Indian Statistical Service, one of India's organised Group A Central Services. The exam tests candidates on subjects including Statistics, General English, and General Studies. The Statistics papers are the most technical and weightage-heavy components of the exam. After the provisional answer key is released and the objection window closes, UPSC reviews all valid representations before publishing the Final Answer Key.

Once the objection period ends, UPSC's subject matter experts review all representations submitted by candidates. Valid objections where an answer is found to be incorrect based on credible references result in changes to the final answer key. The Final Answer Key is then published on the official website. You'll own inbound leads from our waitlist and referrals, respond fast, and make sure no good lead goes cold.
